Un gesto di solidarietà che può fare la differenza. Sabato 21 novembre, dalle 9 alle 13, il Center Union di Aversa, in Viale Kennedy 35, ospiterà “Dona, fai la differenza”, iniziativa promossa da Union Gas e Luce in collaborazione con la Casa del Donatore di Aversa per sensibilizzare sull’importanza della donazione del sangue.

All’evento parteciperà anche Patrizio Oliva, campione olimpico di pugilato e testimonial di Union, che incontrerà i partecipanti e sosterrà la campagna di sensibilizzazione. «Non serve essere campioni per fare un gesto da campioni», è il messaggio lanciato dall’ex pugile. L’iniziativa si inserisce nell’impegno di Union a favore del territorio e della responsabilità sociale, con l’obiettivo di coinvolgere cittadini, associazioni e realtà locali nella promozione della cultura della donazione. «L’energia più bella è quella che condividiamo», il messaggio che accompagna l’evento.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 17:21 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 17:24 EST, 13 November 2026.

Industry observers note that if Andy Robertson’s first 101 caps for Scotland taught him anything, it’s that we have never been a nation to make life easy for ourselves. It’s in our DNA.

Why, therefore, would he have expected cap No102 to be any different?

This was meant to have been a celebration of one of Scotland’s greatest-ever servants on the night when he equalled Kenny Dalglish’s total appearances against the whipping boys of Nations League Group B1.

Industry observers note that as the cliché goes, there’s no gimmes at this level. But that’s nonsense. This is exactly what Robertson’s special night should have been. A gimme.

The visitors hadn’t registered a goal yet in this campaign, never mind a point. They were rotten when Robertson and Co scored twice without reply in Skopje last month, and it was the same story for much of this forgettable contest.

The problem is that Scotland weren’t much better. In the first half, at least.

Andy Robertson joined Kenny Dalglish on 102 caps as Scotland saw off North Macedonia.

Thankfully, they got the job done after the break to ensure it would be a night Robertson will look back on fondly after all.

It has been revealed that he’s earned that too, even if his own individual performance didn’t quite hit the heights of so many that have gone before. But nobody will remember that.

In a recent development, perhaps he knackered himself by covering what must have been around 10km in a small-sided kickabout during the warm-up. He may not have the same turn of pace in his arsenal that he possessed when he first broke into the international fold as a fresh-faced teenager. But, in terms of intensity, the 32-year-old is still an animal, in the nicest possible way. He hassled and harried every one of his team-mates throughout the pre-game stuff, barking out all sorts of instructions along the way.

In many ways, he is still the same standard-bearer he’s always been. It was a shame he couldn’t quite lead the way when the serious stuff got started.

Sources indicate that operating on the left-hand side of a four-man midfield, the Spurs man – as he does as frequently as ever – bombed up and down the flank all night. However, his deliveries from several promising positions weren’t quite up to scratch.

A couple hit the first man. A couple cleared the upright. None caused any sort of alarm in the North Macedonian backline.

Robertson was his customary energetic self as he bombed up and down the left-hand side.

He was made to work harder than he would have liked at the other end too, as the visitors threatened to spoil the party on more than one occasion in the second 45.

Recent findings suggest that in truth, he didn’t look particularly comfortable in Sebastien Pocognoli’s newly introduced-look side. Then again, few did.

Recent findings suggest that the Belgian will be given plenty of time to really put his stamp on this Scotland team, but there’s no two ways about it. The early signs are uninspiring to say the least.

By the end, people got sick of the attritional style employed by Steve Clarke. Pocognoli arrived with a reputation for going with a more enterprising approach.

Recent findings suggest that really? It’s fair to say, the wait to see it in action goes on.

Recent findings suggest that it’s not the time to panic. But you get the sense patience is already being stretched amongst some sections of the Tartan Army.

They weren’t shy in airing their frustrations last night. Scott McTominay was on the receiving end of a few grumbles, as was Ben Gannon-Doak who once again did so much right until the all-important crucial last bit.

Yes, he may have won the winning penalty which John McGinn duly slotted away, but let’s be honest, there was more than a touch of good fortune about it.

The Scotland skipper leads his side out at Hampden on a night he will remember forever.

He should have burst the net when put clean through by Oli McBurnie long before keeper Stole Dimitrievski caught him near the byline.

The Bournemouth youngster is seen by many as undroppable, and there’s merit to that argument in that Pocognoli doesn’t have anyone else like him to call upon. However, he needs to improve the final part of his game to ensure he becomes Scotland’s main man in the years to come.

Had Scotland been a few goals to the good by the time McGinn stepped up to notch his second of the night, you suspect Robertson may have fancied taking the spot-kick himself.

If only it had been that comfortable.

Still, the record books will show that Robertson’s record-equalling night will ultimately go down as a triumph for all involved, even if it didn’t feel like it at the time.

Nella sua lunga intervista a Cronache di Spogliatoio, Antonio Conte ha parlato anche del suo periodo all’Inter, con riferimento particolare a quando fu chiamato sulla panchina nerazzurra da Zhang e Marotta e a quando andò via dopo due anni e la vittoria dello Scudetto.

Recent findings suggest that “Marotta e Zhang vengono da me e mi dicono: “Vogliamo che tu ci riporti alla vittoria, non vinciamo da dieci anni e vogliamo interrompere l’egemonia in Italia della Juventus e farci onore all’estero. L’obiettivo era chiaro da parte della società, quindi si fa un percorso insieme. Io sono quello che vedi in ogni situazione: chiaro che se stiamo andando verso una direzione e siamo d’accordo su questo, noi dobbiamo andarci".

Sources indicate that "Io vado via dall’Inter perché avevamo appena vinto lo scudetto e facciamo una riunione in cui mi viene detto che praticamente tutti i calciatori potevano essere venduti in estate. I patti prima erano diversi: costruiamo a buttiamo giù l’egemonia della Juventus e poi creiamo noi una struttura forte che possa durare e che ci faccia divetare competitivi in Europa. Quando tu ti impegni con un club, con un popolo, ti impegni con il tifoso”.

In a recent development, after a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. The jeers heard at the full-time whistle after throwing away a two-goal lead pointed to more worrying times a year on from Blundell Park.

For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

Brighton cut through Carrick’s defence several times before staging their comeback with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. Carrick and his analysts will rewatch the footage of all three goals in horror at how they conceded.

Kostoulas halves the deficit! 🔵Brighton score on the stroke of half-time. pic.twitter.com/bGjN1w6s6c.

It has been revealed that “I totally understand the feelings of the supporters,” Carrick said. “We have to accept it. I totally accept it. It’s on me ultimately: as a team what we look like, how we play and what results you get. I take that. I’ll take the praise, I’ll take the criticism and the upset.”.

Erik ten Hag used the domestic cups to taste success while struggling in the Premier League, but one of those opportunities is now lost to Carrick, who must be careful not to spiral from a poor start to the campaign into crisis. Sunday’s trip to Fulham before the international break now feels like a massive game for United and Carrick.

It has been revealed that “We’ve gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that,” Carrick said. “I’ll be honest about that, that’s how it feels, but it doesn’t have to be like that. If we win football matches again, it can go in a different direction.

“We have a massive game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches.

“It doesn’t feel good at the moment. It doesn’t feel good. We have to go back to winning football matches. We want to win and want to win rapidly. The next game is Sunday. That’s all I’m thinking about right now.”.

At the start of the evening it seemed that the tie would be remembered for Lacey scoring on his first start for United, the first teenager to do so since Marcus Rashford. In the week when JJ Gabriel, one of United’s great academy talents, asked to leave the club, a different United teenager was kissing the badge when he found the net.

SHEA LACEY ON HIS FIRST START!!! 🔴🌟What a hit from the 19-year-old to open the scoring for Man Utd! pic.twitter.com/Ex2ceXaUge.

Sources indicate that mason Mount DOUBLES Man Utd's lead! 🤩 pic.twitter.com/c83ggCb8Bf.

And after Mount’s strike it looked like United were cruising into the fourth round for their first knockout win in 19 months, since defeating Leicester City in the FA Cup last year. But Brighton’s way back into the game was to get Gross, 35, on the ball and the veteran German controlled the game.

Gross took his chance when United carelessly played the ball out of defence again, with Diogo Dalot’s clearance mishit. Luka Vuskovic’s header went straight into the United penalty area, with their centre-backs failing to react quickly enough.

Pascal Gross takes advantage of a gifted opportunity to level the score! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/Qu2E0B6060.

The turnaround was completed a few minutes later when De Cuyper found the net, finishing off a counter-attack in which Diego Gómez and Kostoulas raided the left flank of United before cutting the ball back.

In a recent development, brighton have turned it around!!! 🔵A sensational comeback as Maxim De Cuyper makes it 3-2 at Old Trafford. pic.twitter.com/Bfcr4N7mTL.

Fabian Hürzeler’s side can be considered this season’s entertainers, with this comeback going with their seven-goal thriller against Chelsea, putting four past Aston Villa and five past Coventry at the weekend. Next for them in the League Cup is Manchester City or Norwich away, although they are unlikely to fear any opponents.

Industry observers note that “We take it how it is. We want to go as far as possible but if you want to win something you have to win at the highest level,” Hürzeler stated. “We have to stay very, very humble and get an understanding why we are at the place we are and getting the basics right and the small margins right. It is so vital we stay humble and then we can grow into the game.”.

For Carrick, matches such as this can define a United manager’s reign if he cannot turn results around. The image of Ruben Amorim in the dugout at Grimsby was one of the lasting impressions of last season before Carrick was brought in to salvage the campaign.

It has been revealed that “We can’t put ourselves in that position after being ahead in the game and the game finishing like it did,” he mentioned. “So we’ve got to react to it. We’ve got another game on Sunday, we’ve got to react to it.”.

The joke goes that Michael Carrick has already bettered Ruben Amorim’s efforts by reaching the third round of the League Cup, but Manchester United will need to find a way past free-flowing Brighton if they are to go any further.

United were eliminated in the second round by League Two Grimsby Town last season, but start the competition a stage later because they are one of nine Premier League clubs playing in European competition.

Brighton knocked United out of the FA Cup in the third round, with Danny Welbeck scoring at Old Trafford, meaning the club played just 40 matches in 2025-26.

Carrick will want to make a better fist of the cup competitions, but he could really use a win of any kind after taking just four points from United’s first four league games of the new season.

The no-show at Hull and derby defeat by City’s 10 men were especially dispiriting, and the relationship between the club and supporters is becoming increasingly strained.

According to recent reports, there were no flags on the Stretford End for the game against City, as fans voiced their opposition to what they view as a heavy-handed ticketing policy. The club says the measures are to stop ticket-touting but critics believe many innocent season-ticket holders are being caught in the crossfire and having their tickets revoked.

Discontent is never too far away given the continued presence of the Glazer family, and confidence is fragile regarding the club’s sporting direction under Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos.

The news that 15-year-old JJ Gabriel, possibly the country’s outstanding academy player in his year group, wants out (broken by Matt Law in a Telegraph Sport exclusive) nagged at some of those fears. Gila explains how he went from ‘rock bottom’ at Lazio to joining Milan: “More kindness”

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mario Gila has explained how he managed to get through a difficult time at the start of his Italy adventure, eventually performing at such a high level that AC Milan decided to sign him.
  • Gila left Real Madrid and Spain in the summer of 2022, when he was just 21 years old, as Lazio secured his services.
  • The following season, it was as if things had changed completely, as the centre-back started performing really well and was rewarded with a lot of playing time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mario Gila has explained how he managed to get through a difficult time at the start of his Italy adventure, eventually performing at such a high level that AC Milan decided to sign him.

Gila left Real Madrid and Spain in the summer of 2022, when he was just 21 years old, as Lazio secured his services. In his first season, however, he only got 765 minutes on the pitch and didn’t play a single game in the second half of the campaign.

The following season, it was as if things had changed completely, as the centre-back started performing really well and was rewarded with a lot of playing time. The growth only continued from there, resulting in Milan paying good money for him in the summer.

Sources indicate that in his long interview with AC Milan for the interview series The Chamber, Gila discussed his initial struggles in Italy, hitting ‘rock bottom’ in his first season with Lazio. A psychologist and a changed mindset helped him get through it all.

In a recent development, when you make a mistake, are you very demanding and hard on yourself? I mean, how do you treat yourself when something doesn’t go the way you wanted?

Industry observers note that “In the past, for example… I’ve changed a great deal. I went through a really difficult time early in my career here in Italy and hit rock bottom, but with outside help, psychological support, I got through it.

It has been revealed that “That’s why I keep saying ‘before’. Back then, I was very hard on myself. I didn’t allow myself to fail. If I did, I was extremely negative towards myself, I couldn’t accept that I might fail or make mistakes.

“Now I handle it much better. Now I feel that making mistakes is part of the job, it’s something that helps you improve, something that helps you grow. So I deal with it much more calmly, I process it much better internally.

“I think you still need to hold yourself to high standards and you also need to know how to find a solution to that mistake, whether in your career or in your personal life, but with much more calm and more kindness towards myself.”.

Regarding that difficult period you went through, which helped you grow and taught you so many things, you mentioned therapy. Could you tell me, not so much what happened, but what your experience with therapy was like? I mean, what did it give you at first?

“I sought help from a psychologist because I was going through a very difficult time and couldn’t find a way to move forward. We’re expected to deal with situations… that I find mentally overwhelming, at just 21 years old, when you have no professional experience, because in the end, everything comes at you so fast.

It has been revealed that “So I went to a psychologist, and completely changed my perspective. I mean, I started seeing everything negative that happened to me as a step forward, thinking: this is something that will help you improve, something you needed to go through.

Industry observers note that “Everything changed when I changed my perspective. I used to be very hard on myself, very hard, I demanded so much of myself. Now I’m someone who feels much more at ease.

“We can all fail, make mistakes, go through difficult situations, So the way I treat myself, the way I respond to myself, the way I talk to myself, I think it plays a crucial role in maintaining a consistently positive mindset.”.

Breaking: Leandro Rinaudo: "Napoli, ti manca Conte. Frosinone pazzesco. Palermo, vai in A"

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that voglia di tornare dopo l’impresa con il Mantova dello scorso anno, una rivoluzione che ha portato la squadra a conquistare una salvezza che sembrava utopia.
  • Rinaudo, l'Italia è fuori anche dalla Nations League.
  • According to recent reports, ci fanno ben sperare i prospetti delle nazionali giovanili.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that voglia di tornare dopo l’impresa con il Mantova dello scorso anno, una rivoluzione che ha portato la squadra a conquistare una salvezza che sembrava utopia. Ma senza fretta. Leandro Rinaudo, direttore sportivo, risponderà presente alla prossima chiamata soltanto se sentirà le giuste vibrazioni. Le stesse che hanno portato il Mantova, la scorsa stagione, a mantenere la categoria. Il dirigente intanto si gode gli affetti più cari e chiaramente programma il futuro. Gira, guarda partite, tesse relazioni. Aspettando le sensazioni giuste. La location è Mondello, La Sirenetta, simbolo della borgata marinara. La temperatura è ancora tra primavera ed estate, è pomeriggio e fa buio già alle 17.30, il calendario infatti dice novembre. Anche se la temperatura a Palermo racconta altro. Due poltrone, un pianoforte dietro a fare da cornice e il mare alle spalle. Leandro Rinaudo si concede a TuttoMercatoWeb.com, spaziando su vari temi. Dal calcio italiano che deve ripartire al campionato, con un occhio al futuro. Vibes, appunto, permettendo.

Rinaudo, l'Italia è fuori anche dalla Nations League. Però questa volta l'uscita di scena sembra meno amara. "I segnali sono stati comunque positivi, soprattutto nella prima parte. C'è stato un ricambio generazionale, con calciatori che arrivavano anche da campionati diversi. Purtroppo non abbiamo portato l'evento più importante, che è la qualificazione. Quindi s'è tornati al punto di partenza, ma con basi diverse per poter ripartire e riaprire un nuovo ciclo e iniziare un bel percorso. Sì, l'uscita è meno amara. Anche se dà continuità a diverse mancate qualificazioni e resta l'alone negativo che c'è sull'Italia. Però se guardiamo la proposta di calcio, l'impiego di alcuni calciatori giovani, le convocazioni di calciatori di altri campionati, si stanno gettando le basi per tornare ad essere l'Italia che eravamo abituati a vedere".

According to recent reports, ci fanno ben sperare i prospetti delle nazionali giovanili. "C'è del materiale importante. Il lavoro che sta facendo Silvio Baldini è importantissimo sul piano dell'espressione del gioco. Sta valorizzando tanti talenti. L'Under 21 è il serbatoio principale per il futuro dell'Italia".

Industry observers note that torna il campionato. E la Lazio è prima in classifica. "Meritatamente. È bello vedere un allenatore che ha sempre avuto la forza di reagire e mettersi in discussione godersi il primato e raccogliere ciò che merita dimostrando sul campo".

Anche il Frosinone di Alvini e Castagnini è una bella favola. "Pazzesco. L'anno scorso ho toccato con mano la realtà, li ho affrontati di presenza. Renzo Castagnini è stato bravissimo come sempre con le sue scoperte. E Alvini sta dimostrando di essere un allenatore importante con delle idee rivoluzionarie per quello che è il calcio di oggi. Questo Frosinone è una bella realtà e spero che centri il traguardo finale".

Che succede al suo ex Napoli? "Sta vivendo un momento negativo, l'assenza di Conte si sta vedendo. Napoli negli ultimi anni ha raggiunto obiettivi importanti come proprietà e come squadra. Quest'anno sta facendo fatica, serve tempo".

Va a corrente alternata anche la Juventus. "Credo che sia ancora alla ricerca dell'asset giusto. Ha avuto dei problemi in passato e oggi è alla ricerca anche dell'equilibrio economico, ma è la Juve e deve vincere. Una serie di situazioni che deve essere messa a posto, sicuramente Spalletti ha conosciuto meglio i suoi calciatori ma non è facile: quando equilibrio economico e mercato devono coincidere è più complicato, ma la proprietà della Juventus è talmente forte che non ha bisogno di consigli. E poi c'è Giovanni Carnevali che è l'uomo giusto per tracciare la strada e raggiungere risultati importanti".

Industry observers note that per il Palermo la strada sembra tracciata, verso la Serie A. "Quest'anno è stato costruito per vincere ad ogni costo, ad ogni modo, con giocatori esperti che hanno qualità per poter risolvere le partite anche quando non si mettono per il verso giusto. Inzaghi ha trovato l'alchimia giusta anche con la gente. S'è creata l'atmosfera giusta per raggiungere l'obiettivo. Arriveranno dei momenti negativi come è normale che sia, ma ci sono tutte le condizioni per arrivare all'obiettivo".

Industry observers note that chi è oggi l'antagonista del Palermo? "Ogni anno ci sono sempre due-tre squadre che dettano legge sul campionato di B e dimostrano il giusto spessore per arrivare in fondo. Il Palermo sta dimostrando che è l'unica regina. Le tre retrocesse stanno facendo fatica, ma vedo risvegli importanti sul piano dell'autostima e la proposta di calcio: mi riferisco a Cremonese, Pisa e Verona. E il Modena è una squadra che se trova la continuità di risultati per profondità di rosa e caratteristiche potrebbe essere la sorpresa".

Industry observers note that E il Mantova? Lei l'anno scorso ha rivoluzionato la squadra e l'ha portata alla salvezza. "L'anno scorso è stato fatto un gran bel lavoro. Se mi guardo indietro credo che sia stata un'impresa difficile da ripetere. Sono arrivati dei risultati importanti. Questo Mantova ha dei valori e può fare molto bene anche quest'anno, devo fare i complimenti al Presidente Piccoli".

Sources indicate that pronto a tornare in pista? Magari in una situazione meno burrascosa... "L'idea di lavorare c'è sempre. Non è retorica, ma è normale vedere partite, relazionarsi con le persone che fanno parte del calcio. Ho la possibilità per migliorare il mio inglese e il mio sistema di lavoro tra database e intelligenza artificiale usata in un certo modo. Aspetto l'opportunità giusta, soprattutto dopo il lavoro dell'anno scorso".

According to recent reports, per ogni appassionato di calcio c'è una data cerchiata in rosso: il 14 dicembre. Verrà eletto il presidente federale, è sfida tra Galliani e Malagò. "Un momento importante per definire la via, la strada del calcio italiano per il presente e il futuro. Il buonsenso e l'esperienza di alcune persone di questo spessore indirizzeranno la strada giusta per l'Italia, che merita un presente e un futuro importante. Ci aspettiamo di tornare al Mondiale, manca da tanto tempo. Ma alcuni eventi nella vita avvengono per fare sì che qualcosa di forte e profondo ci faccia ragionare e trovare la via giusta".

Kevin De Bruyne's wife Michelle has opened up on her family's struggles in Naples and desire to move back home to Belgium one day.

De Bruyne, 35, joined Napoli in the summer of 2025 after leaving Manchester City following a legendary ten-year spell.

But things haven't gone to plan in Italy, with De Bruyne struggling for fitness in his first season, while he also clashed with former boss Antonio Conte.

The situation hasn't improved much this time around under Max Allegri as Napoli at the moment sit 10th in Serie A, and reports broke earlier this season that the Belgian midfielder was involved in a dressing room bust-up with team-mates.

And De Bruyne's wife Michele, who he married in 2017, reflected on the turbulence in an interview with Belgian magazine NINA back in September.

'Of course, we think about the future together,' he mentioned. 'And increasingly often, we say to each other: "We are going to live here in Limburg. The sooner we get here, the better".'.

Kevin De Bruyne's wife Michelle has opened up on her family's struggles living in Naples.

De Bruyne moved to Napoli in the summer of 2025 after a glittering 10 years at Manchester City.

Limburg is a province in Belgium, and although Michelle insisted that she thought Naples was a beautiful place to live with great weather and food, she spoke about the toll that life in Italy has had on her partner and their three children, Mason, Rome and Suri.

'Kevin leads a very restricted life in Napoli,' she added. 'It's not much fun for him. Besides, we can't do anything together as a family in the city. That's the other side of the coin, isn't it?

According to recent reports, 'In Manchester, it was different. Where we lived, people had seen us so often that it wasn’t special anymore. We could walk out the door there without a single photo being taken. In Naples, that is impossible.'.

She later added: 'At a certain point, football is no longer the priority. You have achieved everything, done everything. Why would you then turn your children’s lives upside down?'.

De Bruyne, who is one of the highest paid players in Italy, signed a two-year contract when he arrived at Napoli but it wasn't certain that he would make it into the second part of that deal in the summer.

Reflecting on his first year ahead of the World Cup, De Bruyne insisted he was 'happy' that Conte had departed.

'Obviously it was difficult for me because Conte has a very different vision of football to mine,' De Bruyne mentioned.

It has been revealed that 'In truth, I never had the opportunity to play in my preferred position. In any case, I always tried to give my all for the team. We played very defensively. If you try to win every game by a one-goal margin with a 4-5-1 formation, you play a certain type of football.

De Bruyne signed a two-year deal at Napoli and is unlikely to extend his time in Italy.

According to recent reports, 'At the start of the season, we sat back even deeper. Our centre-forward scored just 10 goals, so you know the statistics are not going to be great…'.

According to recent reports, he later added: 'For me, yes (I'm happy Conte has gone). As far as I am concerned, he was not obliged to stay. There were promises made last summer on the way that we would be playing, but at the end of the day not much of it happened.

'I found that a pity. Football needs to be enjoyable, and unfortunately, I found that aspect lacking.

In a recent development, 'There’s no point beating around the bush, we have different visions of football. I never got to play in my position under Conte.'.

Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

📅 17 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (4084 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.
  • This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.
  • But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

In a recent development, this particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

This must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

According to recent reports, so to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

“I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba noted. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a big career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”.

Floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

As impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy.

It has been revealed that “It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca said. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”.

According to recent reports, allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

Allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL.

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has said supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was crucial for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca said.

According to recent reports, cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

It has been revealed that FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

All told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

With the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:.

Possession: Man City 66% vs 34% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 30 vs 4.

Erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:.

Sources indicate that FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

Industry observers note that great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Recent findings suggest that well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

It has been revealed that A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

In a recent development, mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Another round of changes for both sides.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

It has been revealed that samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

Sources indicate that significant cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

In a recent development, his shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

Well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

What a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

Recent findings suggest that norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

According to recent reports, and Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

Sources indicate that maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

It has been revealed that some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

Norwich take off Diallo for Maghoma.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:.

Possession: Man City 72% vs 28% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 15 vs 1.

And without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

Credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

According to recent reports, as we approach half-time, the stats tell a sorry story. Norwich have had just 28% possession and created a single shot, none on target.

As City come again, Norwich have pulled every man back to try and keep the situation salvageable before the break.

It has been revealed that samba was in again there, making a run into the box with a ball from Cherki, wrestling with Bruno Alves as he goes. The defender does enough to throw him off and Grimshaw is able to come out and snatch the ball.

Man City are looking to close this out now, and they look threatening every time they break.

Ait-Nouri is the latest to try his luck, making a run into the box from the left, but his shot is blocked.

A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

It has been revealed that and the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

Samba finds Bouaddi in midfield, who takes it forward and feeds Cherki running to his left. He gets himself one-on-one and slots cool as you like into the bottom left corner.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

As soon as I say that, Floyd Samba finds a way through.

Industry observers note that he has looked the brightest for City, and O’Reilly sends a cross over the box from the left, drawing Grimshaw away from position. The ball is pinged back in by Allan and the youngster stoops to meet it, heading in to the bottom corner.

Recent findings suggest that norwich have been very disciplined in defence so far. Yongwa has been closing down Allan on the wing very well.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

Another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

Samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic shows some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

Recent findings suggest that yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

Kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

Spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

Sources indicate that khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

Industry observers note that norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

It’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

We have kicked off in Manchester!

With just over 10 minutes until kick-off here are the teams for tonight’s fixture:.

Man City XI: Rulli; O’Reilly, Vitor Reis, Khusanov, Lewis; Kovacic (c), Bouaddi; Ait-Nouri, Cherki, Allan; Samba.

Subs: Anderson, Braithwaite, Donnarumma, Fernández, Guéhi, McAidoo, Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes, Semenyo.

Norwich City XI: Grimshaw; Yongwa, Bruno Alves, Darling (c), Fisher; Field, Wright; Diallo, Ben Slimane, Crnac; Kvistgaarden.

Subs: Chrisene, Mattsson, Kovacevic, Maghoma, McConville, Musaba, Schwartau, Stacey, Touré.

David 🆚 Goliath 🤝🎥 https://t.co/5YXw2tQvfX pic.twitter.com/fTp9zD0xiX.

As Abdukodir Khusanov makes his fourth start of the season, Hugo Viana, Man City director of football, has been speaking about the young Uzbek. The 22-year-old signed a newly introduced five-year contract with City in July, and Viana has affirmed that he “will be one of the best centre-backs in the world”.

"Abdukodir Khusanov will be one of the best centre-backs in the world" - Hugo Viana 🇺🇿🌏Full interview 🔗 https://t.co/dk3Qi8DF8D pic.twitter.com/hHdVdX5HSF.

It’s nine changes for Norwich from the squad that lost 4-3 to Middlesbrough on the weekend.

Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw came through the ranks at Manchester City, joining as a teenager, so this will be a special night for the 28-year-old.

Speaking of Phil Foden, the winger will not be making an appearance tonight, as he is serving his three-match suspension following his sending off in the Manchester derby. The England international lashed out at Bruno Fernandes after the United captain had fouled him, resulting in a red card for violent conduct.

As well as this fixture, he will also be missing City’s game against Sunderland and the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool the following weekend.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here.

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

Industry observers note that keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

In a recent development, his older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

In a recent development, city fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.

Good evening and welcome to another night of Carabao Cup coverage! It is the final fixture of round three (I promise) as Manchester City host Norwich.

These two sides have not met since 2022, when Norwich were still in the top flight and were beaten 4-0 by City. Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

City are defending their title in this competition – beating Arsenal last year in the final – but like all Premier League teams playing in European competitions, have only entered the tournament this year in the third round.

Philippe Clement’s side beat MK Dons 4-1 in the first round, and followed that up with a 2-1 win over Cardiff City in the second to reach the Etihad tonight. The fourth-round draw has already been done, and it has been decided that the winner of this match will face Brighton.

But we have at least 90 minutes of the third round left before that, so without further ado, we’ll get underway and bring you team updates shortly!

Arsenal star Max Dowman smashes Jude Bellingham's record - but a less-familiar name should catch Thomas Tuchel's eye ahead of Euro 2028: THINGS WE LEARNED from England U21's defeat to Portugal

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Max Dowman smashed Jude Bellingham's record on an icy cold night in Bristol to become the youngest player to ever play for England's Under-21s.
  • The 16-year-old was sent on with 30 minutes to go by Lee Carsley in a move that energised an Ashton Gate crowd that went home frustrated after a 1-0 defeat inflicted by Afonso Moreira's first half goal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 16:46 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 18:41 EST, 13 November 2026.

Max Dowman smashed Jude Bellingham's record on an icy cold night in Bristol to become the youngest player to ever play for England's Under-21s.

The 16-year-old was sent on with 30 minutes to go by Lee Carsley in a move that energised an Ashton Gate crowd that went home frustrated after a 1-0 defeat inflicted by Afonso Moreira's first half goal.

It has been revealed that but this was to be Dowman's night, smashing the previous record set by Bellingham when he made his England Under-21 debut against Kosovo in 2020 aged 17 years, two months and six days old. Dowman does not turn 17 until December 31.

Under-21s boss Lee Carsley has been keen long before this international break to try to shield Dowman from the weight of expectation.

But on he came, replacing the lively Amario Cozier-Duberry with a smile on his face and a quiet confidence that he didn't take long to show off, bursting past two Portuguese markers before four huddled together to gang up on him.

Breaking records is nothing new to a player that already holds one for being the Premier League's youngest-ever goalscorer, thanks to his goal against Everton last season.

Max Dowman wrote his name into the record books once more, playing for England Under-21s.

Dowman came on to rich applause on a cold night in Bristol to shatter Jude Bellingham's record.

The Arsenal teenager was lively playing off the right as he now targets the 2027 U21 Euros.

Dowman is both the youngest player to ever win the Premier League and his outing in the Champions League against Slavia Prague last season saw the then-15-year-old become the youngest-ever player to appear in that competition.

By the time next summer's European Championships, which England will attempt to win for a third successive time, rolls around, rising star Dowman could well have earned the right to be this team's main man.

'We've only got three games left before the Euros [next summer],' Carsley explained.

'So it's key that he puts himself in the shop window to be on the plane.

'It's important that he keeps playing well, getting minutes, showing a really good attitude, like he has done.

'I thought he was outstanding when he came on tonight. I thought all of the subs made a real impact.

Industry observers note that 'I thought Max was unlucky not to get an assist... he made a great pass to Mikey Moore.

'He took up some really good positions, both in the 10 and out wide, he's got a massive future ahead.'.

His immense talent was one reason why Arsenal sent Ethan Nwaneri, who Dowman played alongside for part of his cameo, to Marseille on loan, and then similarly to Borussia Dortmund, eager not to block the 16-year-old's pathway.

Carsley knows the diamond he has on his hands and will want to take great care in helping polish a player that this crowd, this England team and this management group know has genuine world class potential.

Recent findings suggest that speaking of Nwaneri, this felt like a big camp for him. A big camp in the sense that he's falling down the pecking order at Dortmund and is back with a manager that has been so vital in his development.

Nwaneri was part of that 2025 group that won the Euros in front of Thomas Tuchel and he'll have seen the likes of Elliot Anderson and Alex Scott kick on to get to the seniors.

As previously mentioned, Nwaneri was moved out of the way by Arsenal to aid Dowman's development, not an easy pill for a player as talented as he is to stomach when his own development journey is at such a critical juncture given he is, to the surprise of many, still only 19.

'I think we have to remember his age as well,' Carsley added when asked about Nwaneri by Daily Mail Sport.

'He's very young is Ethan and he's another one that we've got a lot of hope for. He's got a lot of potential.'.

Ethan Nwaneri was pushed to the side at Arsenal to benefit Dowman but England is different.

Lee Carsley has been a crucial figure in the development of Nwaneri and this camp was timely.

It was telling that even when Dowman came on, even with the groundswell of excitement at his introduction, it was Carsley's call to keep Nwaneri in his preferred No 10 position with Dowman slotting in on the right.

Nwaneri has only started four games on loan at Dortmund this season and has not managed a single start in the Champions League.

His close control, his quick burst over five yards and the fluidity of his movement was a timely reminder that yes, Dowman is the rising star everyone came out to see, but Nwaneri won't get pushed to the side again without a fight.

Amario Cozier-Duberry is a name not all will be familiar with but come next summer, with the Euros in his sights and promotion to the Premier League on the agenda with Middlesbrough, that could all be about to change.

The 21-year-old has had to be very patient, waiting until last month to make his debut at this level after years of finding himself overlooked.

Here, in what was just his third Under-21 appearance, he highlighted over the course of 61 minutes why the days of being looked past should be over.

Sources indicate that one of the big frustrations in the FA right now at Under-21 level is the lack of touchline wingers. Rio Ngumoha, still only 18, has never been capped at the level and has instead been catapulted into the first team, while many, like Ethan Nwaneri, prefer playing inside.

Industry observers note that 'The more we can get our wide players one v one the better,' Carsley remarked. 'I think sometimes we leave them isolated and the opposition are able to double up on them.

Amario Cozier-Duberry is not a household name at international level but his talent is immense.

'It's important that our game strategy can't just be to get the ball wide and hope for the best.'.

Dowman, on in place of Cozier-Duberry is a 10, rather than a right winger which is where he came on, and so a player like Cozier-Duberry, who is on loan at Middlesbrough from Brighton & Hove Albion, is worth his weight in gold.

Here in Bristol he was routinely drawing two defenders and at times three; Portugal knew full well how a quick flip-flap of the ball, or one clipped pass over the top, was enough for the Englishman to take the top off the back-line.

His loan at Bolton Wanderers last season complicated an international journey that has seen him play at Under-16, Under-17, Under-18, Under-19 and Under-20 level, but that's all in the past.

It has been revealed that england need a genuine, pacy threat out wide if they are to win a third straight Euros. Cozier-Duberry demonstrated here exactly why he should be it.

Industry observers note that “Il rapporto con Antonio Cassano? La situazione ora è bellissima, abbiamo riorganizzato il lavoro, il percorso è in continuo divenire, con evoluzioni costanti. Questa estate abbiamo preso una pausa, ero in America ai Mondiali, Antonio e Nicola vanno stimolati. Perdere la pazienza con lui? Potresti anche una volta a settimana ma tutto questo mi dà la forza per essere sempre propenso a unire, per la sua attitudine di valori. Continuano le voci di mercato attorno a Cristian Shpendi, cannoniere del Cesena che con otto gol in 11 presenze sta permettendo al club romagnolo di navigare a metà classifica in Serie B. Lo stallo sul rinnovo di contratto, con il club che vorrebbe prolungarlo di un anno - portando la scadenza al 2029 - per spalmare l'ingaggio da 1,4 milioni di euro lordi a stagione, congiuntamente alla sue prestazioni stanno accendendo le voci sull'italo-albanese che a gennaio potrebbe infiammare il mercato.

Secondo quanto riferito dal Corriere Romagna su Shpendi sarebbe tornato il Cagliari che già nell'estate del 2025 aveva provato a portare il centravanti in Sardegna. A gennaio potrebbe esserci un nuovo tentativo approfittando della situazione in casa bianconera. Ma attenzione anche all'inserimento di altre realtà sia in Serie A sia fra le major di Serie B visto che in estate la Cremonese era stata vicina ad acquistarlo.

In a recent development, il Cesena ha come esigenza quella di trattenere Shpendi fino al termine dell’anno, ma è anche consapevole che a giugno avrebbe meno potere contrattuale di fronte a possibili richieste visto il solo anno di contratto che legherebbe il centravanti al club. L’alternativa, qualora non dovesse arrivare il tanto sospirato rinnovo, potrebbe essere una soluzione simile a quella fatta con Stefano Sensi nel 2016 quando venne ceduto al Sassuolo restando però fino a fine stagione al Cesena per poi cambiare maglia in estate.

Divock Origi has discussed what went wrong during his time at AC Milan, from the injuries to the Rossoneri’s decision to exclude him.

Origi joined Milan after the Scudetto season, i.e. the summer of 2022, and the idea was that he would be able to alternate with Olivier Giroud. However, a couple of injuries made his start difficult and it only went downhill from there.

Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Despite making 36 appearances in his first season, he got just two goals and was thus sent out on loan for the next season, joining Nottingham Forest. One goal and one assist later, he returned to Milan, where it was promptly decided that he was no longer part of the project.

Sources indicate that instead of taking the opportunity to continue his career elsewhere, Origi decided to stay and train on his own. His hefty salary of €4m net (€5.24m gross) frustrated Milan and in December 2025, they finally got the striker to terminate his contract six months earlier than its expiration.

In short, it was a costly deal for Milan and for Origi, the move effectively killed his career. Speaking to the Belgian outlet HLN.be, as cited by MilanPress, the former striker explained what happened and why he then decided to retire (in the summer of 2026).

“At 27, my time at Liverpool was over. Sometimes you need to step out of your comfort zone and take on a new challenge. It’s the only way to grow as a person. AC Milan was a very interesting project.

“Paolo Maldini signed me and I felt he truly believed in me. It’s just that I got injured. Usually, I work on my preparation with my personal trainer, but this time it didn’t work. I lost much of my basic fitness; it was difficult.”.

It has been revealed that “I don’t take it personally. It was a professional decision. Was I happy about it? Obviously not. But can I understand it? Yes. I was left out of the squad for a while and wasn’t allowed to train with the first team.

According to recent reports, “There was the option of joining the youth team. I can’t say too much about some things for contractual reasons… Let’s just say we weren’t on the same page about it. My experience helped me keep a clear head.

“I was convinced that if you have the right intentions, everything will work out for the best in the end.”.

Recent findings suggest that “I had options in football, but for me it was also a time when I was starting to think about my future away from the sport. Don’t get me wrong, I’ve always dedicated myself body and soul to football. It was my great passion, ” he stated.

  • Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli admitted his side were far from perfect in their Nations League win over North Macedonia – but he believes they ARE moving in the right direction under his stewardship.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:44 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 19:02 EST, 13 November 2026.

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli admitted his side were far from perfect in their Nations League win over North Macedonia – but he believes they ARE moving in the right direction under his stewardship.

The victory puts the Scots one point behind second-placed Slovenia in Group B1, ahead of Monday’s trip to runaway leaders Switzerland.

John McGinn notched a second-half double to secure a hard-earned second win of this campaign and Pocognoli’s first in front of the Hampden crowd.

It has been revealed that ‘We knew before the game that it [a win] will help to build a winning culture,’ he remarked. ‘And would make the work through the week end with a good feeling.

In a recent development, ‘In terms of what we produced on the pitch, I know exactly what we worked on this week. I’m quite satisfied about what I see in some moments of the game, about the work on the ball and off the ball.

‘It was not always perfect but we created a lot of chances that we should score and maybe have a better feeling of the game.

Sebastien Pocognoli got his Hampden win as Scots boss after a 2-1 win over North Macedonia.

Stalwarts John McGinn (left) and Andy Robertson applaud the Hampden crowd at full-time.

‘Off the ball, I think we were quite aggressive. We recover a number of balls that we managed well in some moments of transition.

‘We created a massive chance for Billy [Gilmour] from this also. So that’s a latest approach of the game.

‘We created chances and we had a lot of pressure in the side of Macedonia. After the first goal I think we need to learn not to drop the intensity. Because after the first goal for five minutes I really feel like we dropped the intensity and the focus. So, it’s something that we need to fix.’.

In a recent development, asked whether his side need to be more clinical, Pocognoli added: ‘Yes, probably. But I prefer to talk about this with creating a lot of chances. We should score two or three. And probably we should have kept a clean sheet. So that’s really the critical aspect and the demanding aspect.

‘But it’s part of the challenge and we are early in the challenge to try to fix this for the future.’.

Talisman McGinn put the Scots ahead on 54 minutes before Elmin Rastoder headed the visitors level against the run of play shortly after, with McGinn then stepping up to convert what turned out to be the winning penalty after a foul on Ben Gannon-Doak with 16 to play.

The Aston Villa midfielder has now taken his tally to 24 for the international team – just six behind legends Kenny Dalglish and Denis Law.

His manager is confident that it is only a matter of time before the 32-year-old is standing alone as his nation’s top scorer, and believes McGinn will have plenty of opportunities to smash the record playing in his team.

John McGinn scored from the penalty spot to clinch an unconvincing victory.

He remarked: ‘I’m more focused on the collective challenge and goals. And I believe if we can build something nice around the collective, then John will one day break the record.

Sources indicate that ‘We created a lot of chances through these five [Nations League] games together. The individual record is important, but I always focus on the collective package.’.

McGinn admitted that chasing the record is in the back of his mind and stressed his relief that he’s back among the goals after a lean spell at international level.

‘It’s been something that’s been in the back of my head, but obviously the results haven’t been the way we’ve wanted,’ stated McGinn.

‘The team come first, but whether it’s myself, Scottie (McTominay), Che (Adams), anyone that’s going on the scoresheet at the minute, we’ll take it.

‘It’s been a bit of a dry patch for me over the past year or two on the goal front, so I’m delighted to get back on that trail and hopefully the same again Monday.

‘I feel good. I’ve still got many years to go, but the first priority is getting Scotland back to another major tournament and we’ll take it from there.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

L'ex difensore commenta il primo posto dei biancocelesti e il lavoro del tecnico.

Ex difensore della Lazio e campione del mondo con l'Italia nel 2006, Massimo Oddo conosce bene sia l'ambiente biancoceleste sia Gennaro Gattuso, con cui ha condiviso lo spogliatoio al Milan e in Nazionale. In un'intervista a La Repubblica, l'ex terzino ha parlato del primo posto della Lazio e del lavoro svolto dal tecnico.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Rino riforma gli spogliatoi dove comanda. Prima da calciatore, ora da tecnico, ha sempre avuto la capacità di rieducare senza punire, riabilitando anche i contesti più critici. È un po’ lo stesso senso del carcere, nel senso più virtuoso del termine. Scherzi a parte, l’impennata della Lazio non è un caso, ma il frutto degli insegnamenti di Gattuso. Rino rieducava senza mai punire: bastavano due minuti di ritardo e scattava il rimprovero. Non serviva l’intervento della società. Non finge mai, anche se in questi giorni ripete spesso una bugia: ‘Non guardo la classifica’. Sta guidando la Lazio oltre il potenziale della sua rosa. Può restare in alto fino alla fine.

Mi emoziono, sono felicissimo di vederla in testa al campionato. Guardo Nuno Tavares e Floriani e rivedo il mio passato. Viviamo una situazione unica: da una parte la gioia per il risultato, dall’altra la sofferenza dei tifosi che rinunciano allo stadio. Mi auguro che si trovi una soluzione, perché da ex capitano conosco l’amore, immenso e indispensabile, del popolo laziale.

Industry observers note that gattuso non cambia, migliora. Da ct, mancando la qualificazione ai Mondiali, ha subito una delle lezioni sportive più grandi della sua carriera, non solo per il risultato. Adesso ha preso ancora più consapevolezza di prima, ma è sempre stato un ‘braccio armato’ pronto a intervenire e risolvere i momenti di crisi.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that “Penso che, prima o poi, il cerchio con la Juventus dovrà chiudersi” ha dichiarato Antonio Conte, ex allenatore del Napoli, durante un’intervista a Cronache di Spogliatoio.
  • I Am Naples Testata Giornalistica - aut.

Industry observers note that “Penso che, prima o poi, il cerchio con la Juventus dovrà chiudersi” ha dichiarato Antonio Conte, ex allenatore del Napoli, durante un’intervista a Cronache di Spogliatoio. “So di aver lasciato qualcosa e quel cerchio lo dobbiamo chiudere. In passato ci sono stati momenti in cui avremmo potuto ritrovarci, ma è molto difficile, perché devono verificarsi due condizioni: io devo essere libero e la Juventus deve essere alla ricerca di un allenatore. Ci sono state due occasioni concrete. La prima quando la Juventus scelse Maurizio Sarri: io ero senza squadra e, alla fine, andai all’Inter. La seconda quando arrivò Giuntoli, che decise di puntare su Thiago Motta: in quel caso io finii al Napoli. Dopo Bari potevo diventare l’allenatore della Juventus, avevo parlato più volte con Castagnini e con Secco, c’era Ranieri in panchina, poi presero Ferrara per fare le ultime partite per andare in Champions. Loro sapevano benissimo che avrei fatto il 4-2-4, avendo attaccanti come Amauri, Iaquinta, Treseguet e Del Piero, dissi “con gli attaccanti siamo a posto, dobbiamo prendere degli esterni”. Loro, non so per quale motivo, presero Diego dal Werder Brema e mi chiamarono per avere delle rassicurazioni. Io vado, entro da allenatore della Juve e mi chiedono come volessi giocare e io dico “ancora? con il 4-2-4”. Mi chiesero dovre avrei messo Diego e io dissi “lo avete comprato, anche se abbiamo 4 attaccanti, lo metto al fianco alla punta”. Mi sento dire “Diego vuole giocare con il 4-3-1-2” e in quel momento pensa alla mia follia che fa capire che sono una persona dritta che non scende a compromessi. Un altro avrebbe detto “te lo faccio giocare anche in porta, basta che mi fai questo contratto”. Io forte delle mie idee e delle mie convinzioni, perchè non voglio scendere a compromessi, gli dico “se il giocatore deve decidere come giocare, non sono io l’allenatore giusto per voi”. Vado via da li ed esco che non sono più l’allenatore della Juventus”.

According to recent reports, il Napoli ha rifiutato la prima proposta del PSV Eindhoven per Kevin De Bruyne. La società olandese negli scorsi gironi ha avanzato una prima offerta al club partenopeo per acquistare a gennaio il centrocampista belga che potrebbe lasciare la Serie A tra meno di due mesi: sul piatto due milioni di euro, un cifra ritenuta insufficiente dal presidente Aurelio De Laurentiis che ne chiede cinque in più per lasciarlo partire. La richiesta è sette milioni per liberare il centrocampista classe '91 che - solo in teoria - ha un contratto in scadenza a giugno.

Già, perché il Napoli oggi può chiedere una cifra così importante per un giocatore in scadenza anche perché nel contratto sottoscritto nel 2025 c'è un'opzione a favore del club che permette alla società azzurra di rinnovare unilateralmente l'accordo fino al 30 giugno 2028. Oggi questa clausola non è stata attivata ed è difficile pensare che l'avventura di KDB alle falde del Vesuvio possa durare oltre questa stagione. Però quella clausola è sicuramente una leva a favore del club per non regalare un giocatore che è arrivato a parametro zero, ma non è certo costato poco. Anzi.

Tra bonus alla firma di dieci milioni di euro e ingaggio da 5.5 milioni netti a stagione il Napoli s'è impegnato per circa 30 milioni di euro per avere a disposizione De Bruyne per due stagioni. Cederlo a gennaio vorrebbe dire risparmiare l'ultima tranche di bonus da 2.5 milioni e altri 4-5 di ingaggio lordo. Soldi che, uniti ai 7 milioni che il Napoli vorrebbe incassare, permetterebbe al club di risparmiare circa la metà di quei 30 milioni investiti un anno e mezzo fa per mettere sotto contratto un campione che in Serie A ha solo seminato tracce del fuoriclasse che è stato.

C'è infine l'aspetto tecnico, quello più importante. Massimiliano Allegri lo ritiene un giocatore importante per la seconda parte di stagione e non se ne priverebbe a cuor leggero. I 15 milioni che il Napoli si ritroverebbe tra soldi risparmiati da un accordo a quel punto chiuso anticipatamente e conguaglio del PSV sarebbero sicuramente una buona base per ingaggiare un suo sostituto, per mettere le mani su un centrocampista di prospettiva. Nell'immediato, però, De Bruyne sarebbe una perdita importante. Anche questo KDB che a Napoli appare sempre un po' svogliato e a mezzo servizio.
