#38075. Why Bukayo Saka's England spot is suddenly under threat: Clocking up the miles has made Arsenal star a fitness concern - while his rival Morgan Rogers is hitting top gear: CRAIG HOPE

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1259 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Why Bukayo Saka's England spot is suddenly under threat: Clocking up the miles has made Arsenal star a fitness concern - while his rival Morgan Rogers is hitting top gear: CRAIG HOPE

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1259 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 08:57 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 09:21 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • Five seasons ago, Bukayo Saka clocked up 3,000 Premier League minutes for Arsenal.
  • In the same week that Rogers, a Manchester City junior, made his only league start during an unhappy loan season on the south coast - in a goalless draw at Peterborough - Saka was scoring in a 3-1 win in the North London derby.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 08:57 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 09:21 EST, 14 November 2026.

Five seasons ago, Bukayo Saka clocked up 3,000 Premier League minutes for Arsenal. Morgan Rogers appeared in just 217 for Bournemouth, then of the Championship. The pair are the same school age. Yet, back then, one was a young man at the very top of the game, the other was a boy wondering where, and how, he would ever get a game.

In the same week that Rogers, a Manchester City junior, made his only league start during an unhappy loan season on the south coast - in a goalless draw at Peterborough - Saka was scoring in a 3-1 win in the North London derby. They were on very different flight paths.

Industry observers note that today, the ascent of Rogers compares with, dare we say it, the gradual descent of Saka. His supporters will contest that trajectory. They can point to his two goals for England in Croatia last month, his hat-trick in the 6-4 World Cup bronze-medal victory over France and, of course, his Premier League winner’s medal. Their argument has merit, as does any that defends a player of such talent.

Except, this is not about ability. It is about durability. It is about mileage and the fear that, at 25 years old, a near 400 career games are weighing heavy. Rogers, quite remarkably, has played 10,000 fewer Premier League minutes. He is, to borrow horse-racing parlance, unexposed and open to improvement.

Recent findings suggest that until three years ago, this was Saka. He started 87 consecutive Premier League games for Arsenal, a club record, and was getting better season on season - seven, 12, 15 and 20 were his goals tallies from 2021 to 2024. He was both the present and future of the England team.

Bukayo Saka's starting spot in the England XI is now under serious threat ahead of Euro 2028.

England are flourishing with Chelsea's Morgan Rogers (right) occupying the right-hand side.

And yet now, increasingly among those who obverse and are close to the England camp - including, you suspect, Thomas Tuchel - there is a feeling of Saka’s presumed starting jersey being under serious threat. In fact, you wonder if the threat has already passed. Does the position on the right of England’s forward line, with a view to Euro 2028, now belong to Rogers?

This, it should be mentioned, is as much about the exceptional development of Rogers, who will again start on the right here in Spain on Sunday night. But there is another, more uncomfortable possibility, and that is of Saka’s very best days belonging to those North London derbies of yesterday, not tomorrow. He is right now injured with a thigh strain and faces several more weeks on the sidelines.

I was in the room with Tuchel at the World Cup pre-camp in Florida when he revealed, to some surprise, ’Bukayo is just not there yet. Some things are missing’. We had assumed Saka was fit after arranging private sessions in the wake of the Champions League final. The head coach, however, said it would be ‘very unlikely’ that Saka, nursing Achilles discomfort, would be able to start and finish all of England’s matches, and so it proved. He did not start and finish any before the France kick-about, a match that should have been played at Miami Beach, not Miami Stadium.

In the days prior to the semi-final against Argentina, Saka told Tuchel and medical staff he was ready to start. Tuchel went with Rogers on the right and Saka was an unused substitute. After his treble three days later, Saka spoke of his frustration with his playing time in North America.

Throughout the tournament, Tuchel rejected the idea of the Arsenal man being ‘the saviour’, as it was put to him by one colleague following the group-stage goalless draw with Ghana.

Sources indicate that ‘I’m not engaging in that,’ he told us. ‘It’s not like Bukayo comes back and everything is solved.’.

Recent findings suggest that and Tuchel was right. Saka did a lot of good - three assists in the tournament proper - but it felt like he was existing in moments, much like at Euro 2024. Gone was that whiplash speed taking him through defensive lines, the drag and dribble that defenders knew was coming but could do little about. Club-mate Noni Madueke had that explosion, just not Saka’s end product. Combine the two and we had a player. It was why, come the semis, Tuchel went with Rogers.

Recurring injuries and setbacks have plagued the Arsenal winger over the past few seasons.

He was once viewed as England's present and future - but has suffered from a gradual decline.

To revisit our Daily Mail Sport tournament ratings, in which Saka scored 6/10, we recorded: ‘Fitness issues should offer some context, but this was a version of Saka unrecognisable from the player we thought was up there with Kane and Bellingham when it came to being a game-changer. He did provide three assists, including a lovely cross for the opener in Mexico, but never appeared to fully trust his body. Has a bit to prove when back to full fitness.’.

According to recent reports, will he ever, though, regain a consistent level of fitness, strength and sharpness that allows him to impact - again, consistently - like he once did? Just last week, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta admitted the club were struggling to identify the underlying reason for injuries which total double figures in three years.

Industry observers note that ‘We have openly discussed a lot of things with him to understand what could possibly have gone wrong,’ noted Arteta. ‘But the reality probably is that unfortunately we don’t know.’.

In a recent development, saka, to return to horse racing, has the form in the book, but that is the concern. There is, perhaps, too much form at too young an age, especially when coupled with a game reliant on acceleration and intensity.

Rogers himself still has a lot to prove, not least because of his £117million transfer from Aston Villa to Chelsea in the summer. With that, though, he has grown. That much was evident by him taking centre stage against Croatia on Thursday night despite the presence of Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham. Previously, you suspected Rogers was waiting for the leading men to hand him his script.

Sources indicate that his tendency to come infield will suit Tuchel, too. Kane the quarterback, as we saw at Wembley, leaves a space to populate and exploit. Rogers had more touches in the penalty area than any other player, including the one for his opening goal. And if Anthony Gordon, on the opposite flank, is the one with chalk on his boots, Rogers muddying his in the goalmouth is what the team needs.

Meanwhile, Rogers has hit top gear at Chelsea and become a key man under Thomas Tuchel.

According to recent reports, this debate, Saka versus Rogers, is not one that should keep Tuchel awake at night. It is a nice problem to have - the hope that Saka will return to his best, the expectation that Rogers is still to realise his.

On Sunday, at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid, Rogers has another opportunity to further his claims. He has come a long way since a drab Wednesday night at Peterborough’s London Road in 2021. It is, though, the distance yet travelled that is most exciting.

Al podcast Passa dal BSMT di Gianluca Gazzoli, l’ex difensore Lele Adani ha parlato così del Como di Cesc Fabregas e non soltanto.

“Serie A in corso? Mi auguravo la ricerca di un calcio offensivo, anche a discapito di qualche errore difensivo. Bisogna esplorare credendo. C’è il Como, c’è il Frosinone, c’è la Lazio. I valori possono tornare, ma non sempre. Mi piacciono i percorsi nuovi, da dieci anni lo sostengo. Pensa l’Atalanta di Gasperini che vince l’Europa League… Nella modernità, nel budget, nel ritorno di tifosi, è difficile fare una cosa così. Accade se hai un percorso di un certo tipo.

Fabregas unisce le aree, tutte le aree lo descrivono come il loro Cruijff. Tutti lavorano per comprenderne pensiero e visione. È riconosciuto ora, ma prima si criticava, è il nuovo che spaventa. Vogliamo fare i conti dei soldi dalle big? La chiave è quanto spendi, senza sprecare però. Ora tu vorresti Paz, Ramon, Da Cunha, Butez, adesso. Prima no, quindi sono le competenze, se vedono solo loro. Sono andato a vedere Como-Torino, sono entrato in spogliatoio, aveva una lucidità che non può esistere dopo una partita. Dopo una gara sono tutti stravolti. Una seduta totale di analisi del match, lucidissimo, appena finita la gara”.

Gerry Cardinale ha promesso grandi investimenti per rinforzare la rosa del Milan. A partire già dal calciomercato di gennaio, quando la rosa sarà, a quanto pare, migliorata con due o tre innesti di alto livello. Uno di questi sarà certamente in attacco, che rimarrà orfano di Francesco Camarda, il quale sarà mandato a giocare in prestito o in Serie B o, addirittura, all'estero. Al posto della punta classe 2008, la dirigenza rossonera potrebbe puntare su un grande colpo, provando ad anticipare l'investimento estivo sull'altra punta già, per l'appunto, a gennaio. I nomi sono due: Endrick del Real Madrid e Nicolò Tresoldi del Club Brugge.

Sources indicate that ma su chi, tra i due, sta puntando ora Gerry Cardinale e perché dovrebbe preferire l'uno all'altro? Intanto partiamo da un assunto: entrambi hanno costi molto importanti, soprattutto per un mercato cosiddetto di riparazione come quello invernale. Endrick costa circa 70 milioni di euro, mentre la valutazione di Tresoldi è schizzata verso l'alto dopo le grandi prestazioni di questo inizio di stagione, volando oltre i 40 milioni di euro. Per il Milan non è un grosso problema di costi. Cardinale, infatti, ha promesso di rinforzare la rosa con i giocatori giusti, utili ad Amorim, anche se questi dovessero prevedere degli esborsi molto alti. D'altronde, una dimostrazione la si è già avuta in estate con gli acquisti a suon di milioni, i più costosi della storia del club rossonero, di Gonçalo Ramos, di Diego Moreira e di Mario Gila. Quindi, il preferire uno all'altro non ha quello economico tra i criteri valutati. È una questione tecnica, è una questione tattica.

According to recent reports, il Milan crede, infatti, che Endrick abbia un potenziale superiore rispetto a Tresoldi ed è dunque il brasiliano la prima scelta. E poi c'è il parametro Amorim. Il tecnico portoghese non ha chiesto una prima punta d'area di rigore, essendoci già Gonçalo Ramos titolarissimo in rosa, ma ha chiesto una seconda punta mobile, mancina, tecnica, di grande qualità, che possa duettare con il portoghese e con Pulisic nell'attacco rossonero. Ecco perché si proverà fino a gennaio a buttar giù le resistenze di Mourinho, offrendo al Real Madrid 60 milioni di euro più 10 di bonus e la possibilità per i Blancos di ricomprare il giocatore entro un paio d'anni a 20-25 milioni di euro in più. Se non ci si dovesse riuscire, c'è sempre l'opzione, comunque molto gradita, di Tresoldi.

E’ andato in scena la prima edizione del premio “Eccellenza Calcistica Italiana”, riconoscimento dedicato alle figure che hanno lasciato il segno nel panorama calcistico nazionale. Tra i vincitori figura anche il vicepresidente della SSC Napoli, Edoardo De Laurentiis, premiato per i meriti conseguiti nell’area della Governance: “E’ per me un grande onore ricevere questo riconoscimento, ma la gioia è doppia per averlo condiviso con mio padre, che è il mio mentore e la mia guida. Ho mosso i primi passi in questo mondo quando ero ancora molto giovane, ho commesso diversi sbagli, ma mi impegno quotidiano per crescere ed essere all’altezza del mio ruolo”.

Industry observers note that successivamente, a margine della cerimonia di premiazione, il vicepresidente ha aggiunto: “La chiave è proseguire giorno dopo giorno con costanza, facendo gruppo. La coesione è fondamentale per raggiungere gli obiettivi prefissati. Diventerà la futura casa del Napoli (riferendosi al nuovo centro sportivo), un luogo in cui far crescere i giovani, costruire il nostro vivaio e scoprire nuovi talenti. Abbiamo vissuto tantissime esperienze entusiasmanti, dall’era Spalletti fino a Conte. La più grande è stata osservare la squadra capace di conquistare costantemente traguardi prestigiosi e di mantenersi sempre ad altissimi livelli”.

Nella Serie A 2025-26 l’olandese aveva segnato quattro reti in 29 presenze; ora conta anche quattro assist.

According to recent reports, tijjani Noslin ha segnato quattro gol e servito quattro assist con la Lazio: per partecipazioni alle reti in Serie A è secondo solo ad Adrien Rabiot. Secondo quanto riportato da Corriere dello Sport, Il francese del Milan conta cinque gol e quattro assist, uno in più dell’olandese nel totale.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

According to recent reports, noslin ha realizzato le sue quattro reti in 10 partite di campionato. Sono tante quante quelle segnate nelle 29 presenze dell’intera Serie A 2025-26. Solo una volta ha fatto meglio, arrivando a cinque gol nella stagione 2023-24.

It has been revealed that il suo percorso da rider a realizzatore si è sviluppato nell’arco di cinque anni, dal 2021 a oggi, passando attraverso difficoltà e successi. Ora i suoi gol e i suoi assist lo collocano tra i giocatori più incisivi del campionato, non soltanto della Lazio.

Il dato più alto di Noslin per partecipazioni alle reti in una stagione di Serie A resta quello del 2023-24. Con l’Hellas Verona, in 17 partite, fu coinvolto in nove gol: cinque segnati e quattro assist.

Con i quattro gol e i quattro assist attuali è a quota otto. Ha dunque già eguagliato il numero di passaggi decisivi registrato in quella stagione, mentre gli manca una partecipazione a una rete per raggiungerne il totale.

  • "Allegri consapevole del gesto “facciamo calcio”?

Al podcast Passa dal BSMT di Gianluca Gazzoli, l’ex difensore Lele Adani ha parlato così del gesto 'facciamo calcio' e di Massimiliano Allegri.

"Allegri consapevole del gesto “facciamo calcio”? Il gesto è nato semplicemente in una camera, l’equivalente dell’idratazione nella camera d’hotel. Lì ero a Francoforte e parlavo dopo una partita dove la Slovacchia batte il Belgio. A un certo punto parlo di Lobotka e dico che fa calcio. E piace, ma il gesto di fare calcio è una cosa che è vecchia come la Bibbia, da sempre, è un gesto. Ma se lo metti lì e non lo guardi, passa come scontato. Per quello mi è piaciuto quando tanti l’hanno preso. È legato al calcio giocato. Se Max lo fa riferendosi ai suoi, lo fa per dire a loro di tenere palla. Poi ci metto il video e le parole giuste, ma bisogna lavorarci. L’attitudine è unire, non separare. Che sia Allegri, Spalletti, Italiano, De Zerbi, Mancini, se vedo un percorso nobile io lo riconosco. Non ho nessun motivo personale per favorire uno o penalizzare un altro. Lo rivendico questo.

In a recent development, sono stato molto critico con De Zerbi negli ultimi mesi, lui è mio fratello. Gli ho detto che il secondo anno a Marsiglia ha fallito e al Tottenham all’inizio ho detto che è stato terrificante, ho esagerato. Io devo premiare Allegri se fa bene e ci avevo sperato io. Lo scorso anno al Milan dicevo che vedevo qualcosa, però se poi è una speranza e non accade, non sarei felice io. Crociata contro Max? Non è così. Molti dicono che sia l’artefice della nuova comunicazione come De Zerbi lo è in campo. De Zerbi nuovo guru del calcio giocato e quello della nuova comunicazione in nome del ‘bel gioco’ che è un concetto vuoto, questo dicono”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that 1 dicembre 2024, a Firenze, al Franchi, si gioca Inter-Fiorentina. Fischio d’inizio alle ore 18. Minuto diciassette, il gioco è fermo. L’arbitro Doveri e la sua squadra stanno revisionando un gol di Lautaro Martinez, poi annullato. Negli Emirati Arabi sono le ore 21. L’agente di Edoardo Bove, Diego Tavano, si trova da quelle parti e guarda la partita sul cellulare. Il segnale si interrompe, Tavano sa che è una partita importante per la Fiorentina ma anche e soprattutto per il suo assistito. Impreca, non sa che di lì a poco, dopo il gol annullato a Lautaro Martinez, Edoardo sta per andare incontro a qualcosa di più grande di lui. Gli arrivano messaggi di conforto sul cellulare, non capisce. Edoardo Bove si china per allacciarsi le scarpe e subito dopo essersi rialzato si accascia per terra. Compagni e avversari richiamano l’attenzione dei sanitari, la situazione sembra già preoccupante a primo impatto. È un arresto cardiaco, Bove corre via in ambulanza. Ricovero in terapia intensiva. Per fortuna, nessun danno di natura neurologica. A Edoardo, nei giorni successivi, viene impiantato un defibrillatore sottocutaneo rimovibile. Amici e familiari si stringono attorno al giovane colpito da qualcosa di più grande di lui. Un calvario che però ha superato brillantemente tornando in campo, in Inghilterra, con la maglia del Watford. Nei cinema di tutta Italia è sbarcato “In un battito”, il documentario che vede Bove protagonista. Un docufilm dal quale, oltre a un ragazzo appassionato e innamorato del pallone, emerge il quadro del procuratore, Diego Tavano, il cui rapporto va ben oltre quello tra un agente e un calciatore. A raccontare l’idea del film, con uno sguardo al futuro di Edoardo Bove, è proprio l’agente a TuttoMercatoWeb.com.

In a recent development, tavano, come è nata l’idea del documentario? “Subito dopo che era fuori pericolo parlavamo con i genitori e con Edoardo, che ha approcciato dicendo: ‘Ma che dici se ci facciamo seguire e vediamo dove arriviamo?’. Così mi sono subito attivato cercando di dargli una mano. Ho chiamato Edoardo Leo, gli ho spiegato l’idea e ci ha messo subito a disposizione una troupe. Tutto ciò che si vede nel film è vero. Reale”.

In a recent development, nel docufilm emerge un ragazzo innamorato del calcio e con delle fragilità dovute al momento. Difficile, solitamente, aprirsi così pubblicamente… “Aveva ventidue anni quando è successo l’incidente, vi posso garantire che mi ha insegnato tante cose nonostante la sua giovane età. Mi ha insegnato ad avere più coraggio, quando gli parli ti dà l’idea di essere un uomo maturo. Solo un ragazzo del genere poteva avere la forza e l’umiltà di spogliarsi completamente di qualsiasi tipo di freno inibitorio e farsi vedere nei momenti di difficoltà e condividere con tutti il messaggio di non mollare. Il suo obiettivo era quello di giocare a calcio, è la sua vita. E con tutte le sue forze è riuscito a tornare in campo. Già prima del film e di tutto ciò che stavamo costruendo sapeva che avrebbe dato un messaggio a tutte le persone che vivono un momento di difficoltà. Voleva far vedere che non bisogna mai mollare, una caratteristica dell’Edoardo calciatore”.

Industry observers note that si guarda indietro e ripensa all’1 dicembre 2024. Cosa le viene in mente? “Quel giorno ero negli Emirati Arabi, lontano. Non l’ho mai raccontato: Edoardo stava facendo bene, era in un momento top e sapevo che era una partita importante. Come mi succede con alcuni dei miei atleti, quando guardo le partite lo faccio con grande tensione. Stavo guardando la partita, a un certo punto salta il segnale. Subito dopo il gol annullato di Lautaro si blocca il segnale, io impreco. Non ho visto in diretta il momento dell’incidente, come un segnale per non farmi soffrire e stare male. E intanto mi arrivavano messaggi del tipo: ‘Facci sapere come sta Edoardo’, oppure ‘Stai tranquillo, non è niente’. Vedo Lautaro fare gol e si stacca la linea. Non poteva essere successo niente, ho pensato che si fosse fatto male a una caviglia o a un ginocchio. Poi mi hanno detto che Edo era andato giù. Inizio a tremare, ero lontano, inerme. Dopo sette-otto minuti è ripartito il collegamento. Non ho visto quello che gli era successo, qualcuno me l’ha voluto risparmiare. Altrimenti sarei caduto insieme a lui”.

Nel film emerge anche il vostro grande rapporto, che va al di là del calcio. “Io e lui ci chiamiamo man. Un giorno vide un mio video di quando ero a New York, chiamai un poliziotto con questo appellativo e lui rise. Era un po’ spiazzato, chiamare un poliziotto Hey man è un po' singolare. Da lì in poi ci chiamiamo così. Il rapporto è pazzesco, tutte le scelte fatte le abbiamo sempre condivise. Quando la Roma ci ha messo alla porta per andare via, mi ha visto lottare contro il club senza alcun freno. Lì mi ha detto che veder lottare qualcuno per lui senza paura gli ha fatto capire che aveva la miglior persona che potesse rappresentarlo”.

A un certo punto, mentre Edoardo doveva fare la visita più importante, a stare male è lei: tachicardia e controllo medico inevitabile “Avevo esagerato con i caffè. Era la visita più importante tra quelle che aveva fatto. Era quella decisiva per capire se potesse giocare in Inghilterra. E avevo scelto di stare fuori dalla stanza, camminavo su e giù. La tensione era talmente tanta che ho avuto un po’ di tachicardia pure io. Ma è finita lì. Il regista è stato bravissimo a montare l’episodio. Mi ero anche spaventato, ma per fortuna tutto bene. Non ho vissuto quel momento come un agente. Edoardo in quel momento era come mio figlio. Si preoccupava per me, la Fiorentina di lì a poco lo avrebbe riscattato e stavo per fare una grande operazione anche io. Ma gli ho detto di non preoccuparsi per me, è più importante averlo vicino come persona. I soldi li rifaremo più avanti”.

Come è nata l’idea Watford? “Gian Luca Nani mi fece una telefonata ad agosto 2025. Ma venivamo da un’operazione che non ci aveva ancora fatto fare lo step per giocare. Gli dissi: ‘Ora non si può, ma teniamola viva’. Nani mi ha dato apertura. Intanto era arrivata un’offerta importante dal Canada. Ma in quel momento non contavano i soldi. Edo ha pensato solo a stare bene e così abbiamo scelto il Watford”.

Ha un contratto con il Watford fino al 2031. Dove immagina Bove l’anno prossimo? “Quest’anno ha iniziato fortissimo. Poi ha avuto un piccolo problema a un ginocchio, ma lo ha superato completamente. Stava facendo bene, è tornato ai suoi livelli. Considerato che la Championship è un calcio differente, ha dovuto adattarsi ma lo sta facendo bene. Se non abbiamo luce verde per l’Italia, arrivare in Premier League sarebbe un sogno. Ma averlo visto esultare e fare gol è stata già una grande emozione”.

Sources indicate that in Italia, al momento, non può giocare per legge. “Come nostra prerogativa siamo uomini che rispettano le leggi e i regolamenti. Poter tornare a giocare in Italia sarebbe un sogno, l’auspicio che qualcosa cambi ovviamente c’è. Ma nel massimo rispetto. Di certo non faremo guerre contro chi pensa che in questo momento sia giusto così. Ma adeguarsi un po’ ai regolamenti che vediamo altrove potrebbe avere un senso, ma non siamo qui a forzare. Edo non ha mai voluto sfruttare questa sua attuale popolarità per chiedere il cambio del regolamento. C’è un disegno di legge, speriamo che il Governo trovi i fondi per la Legge Bove così da preparare più persone al primo soccorso. E colgo l’occasione per ringraziare il Senatore Marco Lombardo, che ci ha aiutato ad entrare nelle sale più importanti della politica per parlarne”.

Cosa le ha insegnato questa storia? “Questa storia mi ha fatto scoprire che nella vita non necessariamente i legami di sangue sono quelli più importanti. Edo è uno di famiglia, come un figlio. Si può amare anche al di fuori della propria famiglia. Sono grato di aver conosciuto un ragazzo del genere, a prescindere dal calciatore. Fa parte delle persone più importanti della mia vita”.

L’ex giocatore biancoceleste e del Milan ha parlato del rapporto con l’amico ed ex compagno di squadra in un’intervista a Repubblica. CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Secondo Oddo, l’esperienza da commissario tecnico della Nazionale, conclusa senza la qualificazione ai Mondiali, ha inciso sulla consapevolezza di Gattuso. Da ct, mancando la qualificazione ai Mondiali, ha subito una delle lezioni sportive più grandi della sua carriera, non solo per il risultato. Adesso ha preso ancora più consapevolezza di prima».

Industry observers note that oddo riconosce nell’allenatore della Lazio un ruolo che aveva già ai tempi del Milan: «ma è sempre stato un “braccio armato” pronto a intervenire e risolvere i momenti di crisi. L’ex compagno precisa: «bastavano due minuti di ritardo – capitava soprattutto ai brasiliani, esclusi Dida e Kakà – e scattava il rimprovero. Non serviva l’intervento della società».

Sources indicate that aurelio De Laurentiis, presidente del Napoli, è stato tra i protagonisti della prima edizione del premio “Eccellenza Calcistica Italiana”, manifestazione dedicata alle personalità che si sono distinte nel panorama calcistico nazionale. L’evento si è svolto a Villa Campolieto, a Ercolano, dove il patron azzurro ha ricevuto un riconoscimento nella categoria Fair Play, che vedeva tra i finalisti anche Andrea Belotti e Luca Percassi. Nel corso del suo intervento, De Laurentiis ha parlato anche del film dedicato al Centenario del Napoli: “La sceneggiatura del film del centenario la scrive il qui presente Maurizio de Giovanni. Il calcio in Inghilterra è nato con gli aristocratici. Non era un fatto popolare. Arrivarono a Napoli e iniziarono a giocare con gli scugnizzi. Il 1922 sembrerebbe la vera data, poi procrastinata al 1926 per la nascita del Napoli. Che non si chiama Società Sportiva, ma Calcio Napoli. Questo film è venuto talmente bene che una piattaforma importante come Amazon lo porterà nel mondo. Quando abbiamo vinto lo Scudetto con Conte, ho fatto un film e sono andato a Los Angeles: presi questo cinema e ho fatto questa anteprima dove sono arrivati questi tifosi dall’America. C’erano donne emozionatissime che dicevano di non capire nulla di calcio ma che si sono comunque fatte trascinare. Ho scoperto che a San Pedro ci sono 30mila tifosi del Napoli legati all’isola d’Ischia”.

#38060. All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper

📅 20 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 29 min read (5877 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~29 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that for all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper.
  • Sources indicate that we keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing?
  • Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that for all the money spent, Tottenham Hotspur have started this season without a reliable out-and-out striker and short of a top goalkeeper. And it is already costing them dear.

Sources indicate that we keep hearing that Dominic Solanke will be the man to give Spurs a goalscoring threat, but how long has it been since we have seen him fully fit and firing? Maybe not since his Bournemouth days.

Antonin Kinsky may have finished last season well, but there was further evidence in this defeat that he is well short of the best goalkeepers in the division.

It is a puzzle how Tottenham signed 10 fresh players, but did not upgrade two of the most vital positions on the pitch.

Only when Aston Villa were out of sight and the game was effectively over did Spurs break their Premier League goal drought. And even then it was a midfielder, Conor Gallagher, and a defender, Jan Paul van Hecke, who were on target.

Solanke had gone off just before Villa scored their second goal, which highlighted the big difference between the two sides on Saturday and where Spurs are badly lacking.

Zion Suzuki, the Villa goalkeeper, launched a long ball upfield, Nicolas Jackson managed to lay it off for Johan Mazambi, who returned the favour. Jackson touched the ball past Micky van de Ven’s challenge before beating Kinsky with a well-struck shot.

Spurs are stunned as Nicolas Jackson doubles Aston Villa's lead 😳📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/il7NKbgFCQ.

It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Asked if Tottenham had made a big mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

It has been revealed that “We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”.

That sounded a bit like excuses, but De Zerbi did not put up much of a defence for Solanke as he noted: “We need more from him, for sure, but he’s one of my players. I like Dom as a player and I stay with him until the end. He needs to stay better, to feel better. The physical condition is not good enough, but it’s normal for him. Maybe he is not confident enough in himself at this moment, because he’s much better than this. I think we can’t say everything is bad, but it’s not enough.”.

It was Sávio who forced Suzuki into making a brilliant double save from him in the first half, when Tottenham were well on top. The Japan international also stopped an Archie Gray shot from squirming through his legs and into the net, and dived to turn another Sávio effort around his right-hand post.

In a recent development, jackson was not the only Villa upcoming boy who upstaged Tottenham’s expensive new attackers. Manzambi not only assisted for Jackson, but also marked his first start for the Midlands club with a goal that put the visitors ahead in first-half stoppage time.

Johan Manzambi is off the mark for Aston Villa, and what a time to do it! ⚽️📺 Stream now on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/rLRbbUM4Jm.

Andrew Robertson will have been disappointed with his attempt to clear the ball, John McGinn played it into the path of Boubacar Kamara and his scuffed shot fell into the path of Manzambi, who found the back of the net.

It has been revealed that good afternoon and welcome to our coverage of today’s bottom-of-the-table epic: Tottenham Hotspur vs Aston Villa. This tie is incidentally the match-up between the last two winners of the Europa League, though so far neither of them have looked like European champions.

It is definitely fair to say that this season has not started the way either of these teams would have wanted, as the host side presently sit in what is apparently their favourite position – 17th – and the visitors are all the way in 19th, only above Coventry.

Despite getting off to a fairly convincing start in the Champions League with a 3-2 win over Club Brugge, Villa only scored their first league goal last week in their match against Nottingham Forest, though it was a futile one as they still lost 2-1 at Villa Park.

Tottenham meanwhile are still waiting for their first league goal, despite putting one past Liverpool in their 3-1 defeat in the Carabao Cup third round. With no European football and already out of one cup competition, Roberto De Zerbi has only the FA Cup in January and the rest of the league season to drag Spurs out of the perpetual rut they appear to find themselves in. They sit only one point above Villa as they have been able to see out two 0-0 draws – against Everton and Nottingham Forest – instead of one.

There has been plenty of talk about the money spent by both teams, without the results yet to show for it. The total sits around half a billion between them, adding to the mounting pressure on both De Zerbi and Unai Emery. Summer signings for both teams have struggled to land, something which will not be helped by the upcoming international break.

Sources indicate that but before then, the teams have 90 minutes to try and get their seasons up and running, and we will be bringing you the team news, lineups and all the action from the match! Stay tuned!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il centrocampista del Venezia, Matteo Dagasso, ha parlato in conferenza stampa a pochi giorni dalla sfida in programma contro la Juventus, a Torino. Reduce dalla chiamata con l'Under 21 di Baldini, il classe 2004 ora punta a trovare spazio anche a livello di club. Ecco di seguito le sue dichiarazioni.

L'ottimo rendimento in Under 21 ti daranno più voglia e determinazione nel chiedere più spazio al Venezia dove non ne hai trovato quanto in Nazionale? "Sono molto contento di come sia andato questo raduno in Nazionale, mi dà fiducia. Anche per motivi fisici ho trovato poco spazio, mi serviva. La cosa più importante ora è che mi sia ripreso da questo mezzo infortunio che ho avuto. Posso allenarmi bene, se il mister mi darà spazio sarò ancora più contento, sono pronto".

In a recent development, se il mister ti darà spazio... ma in che ruolo? Con Stroppa eri playmaker, Nicola forse ti vede più mezzala... "Io ho voglia di giocare. Che sia da play o da mezzala è indifferente. Forse mi piace un po' di più fare la mezzala, ma per me è uguale".

In a recent development, come ti trovi con Nicola? Cosa ti chiede e in cosa vedi cambiata la squadra? "Mi trovo molto bene con il mister. Da mezzala mi chiede di buttarmi nello spazio, un po' le richieste che ho anche in Nazionale e mi trovo bene da questo punto di vista. Come squadra ci siamo adattati bene a questo cambio. Stiamo lavorando forte, l'unica cosa importante da fare".

It has been revealed that ora la Juve: cosa serve per fare punti a Torino? "Una partita bellissima. Per fare punti dobbiamo fare quello che sappiamo fare, stiamo preparando la partita e cercheremo di applicare al meglio i concetti che ci chiede il mister".

L'infortunio arrivato dopo il Lecce ti ha condizionato? Cosa è successo? "Ho avuto un problemino prima del Lecce, in Coppa Italia, contro il Modena, per il quale sono stato fermo 4-5 giorni. Poi ho giocato contro Lecce e Udinese e ho avuto questo problemino al flessore che mi ha tenuto fermo un mese abbondante. Ora mi sento bene ed è quello l'importante".

Nicola ti ha elogiato. Cosa ti chiede nello specifico e cosa è cambiato rispetto a Stroppa? "Come dicevo mi chiede di inserirmi, come alle altre mezzali. Sulle differenze: con mister Stroppa c'era più un gioco di palleggio, con mister Nicola invece un gioco un po' più verticale".

Che consigli vi danno giocatori come Juan Jesus, Busio e Kike Perez? "Sono fondamentali sia per indirizzare noi giovani, hai citato Kike, Juan e Busio ma personalmente mi ha aiutato tanto anche Alfred (Duncan, n.d.r.). Sono fondamentali sia per i consigli in campo che fuori, per gestire certe situazioni".

According to recent reports, per quali caratteristiche dovrebbe puntare su di te il mister? "Mi piace avere la palla fra i piedi, ma anche inserirmi e pressare. Queste sono le mie caratteristiche principali".

Hai giocato circa 110 minuti fino a qui. Al netto dell'infortunio e della concorrenza, ci sono altre motivazioni? "Non lo so, non sono domande cui devo rispondere io, penso. Io mi sono allenato sempre bene quando sono stato disponibile, a centrocampo ci sono tanti giocatori forti, è una sana competizione e questo mi spinge a dare ancora di più, è un punto di forza per la squadra. Come dicevo per me l'importante era rimettermi a posto fisicamente e da circa un mese sto bene. Se il mister mi darà spazio sarò pronto".

Senti di dover ancora fare esperienza in Serie A? "L'esperienza penso che si acquisisca soltanto giocando, per un ragazzo della mia età penso sia fondamentale. Ma io penso solo ad andare in campo e a dare il massimo, per il resto non dipende da me".

Recent findings suggest that come vedi il gruppo squadra del Venezia, sia a livello tecnico che umano? "Per me siamo una squadra forte. All'inizio ci sono stati tanti nuovi acquisti, tanti nuovi, per il gruppo quindi ci è voluto un attimo per conoscerci meglio. Ora ci siamo e anche i risultati lo stanno dimostrando".

#38057. Former Rangers striker Peter van Vossen on THAT Old Firm miss 30 years ago today... 'I wasn't paying attention and the ball hit my shin, but I still blame Jorg Albertz!'

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2183 w)

Former Rangers striker Peter van Vossen on THAT Old Firm miss 30 years ago today... 'I wasn't paying attention and the ball hit my shin, but I still blame Jorg Albertz!'

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2183 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 09:41 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 09:44 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • In a career spanning almost 20 years, Peter van Vossen won the Champions League, made it to the quarter-finals of the World Cup with his country and won league titles in both the Netherlands and Scotland.
  • Point being, it’s reductive to define his time in football by one excruciating miss.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 09:41 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 09:44 EST, 14 November 2026.

In a career spanning almost 20 years, Peter van Vossen won the Champions League, made it to the quarter-finals of the World Cup with his country and won league titles in both the Netherlands and Scotland.

Point being, it’s reductive to define his time in football by one excruciating miss. But here we are.

It’s 30 years to the day since Van Vossen missed an open goal for Rangers during a crucial Old Firm clash at Celtic Park. Leading 1-0 and with less than seven minutes remaining, the Dutch forward had a chance to seal all three points for the nine-in-a-row-chasing Light Blues. Instead, he blazed over with the goal at his mercy.

According to recent reports, in the decades since, the spurned chance has become the benchmark by which all other misses have been measured. ‘Sure, it was bad — but was it “Van Vossen” bad?’.

The man himself has seldom spoken about the events of that powder keg of a night. Until now. Living the quiet life in rural Holland, Van Vossen has given Daily Mail Sport a full account of his professional nadir.

According to recent reports, ‘I mostly remember being mad at Jorg [Albertz],’ he indicates. ‘I was seriously p***** off with him. Paul Gascoigne played a pass inside to me and I clipped a first-time ball in behind the Celtic defence, who were pressing high. If Jorg had just left it, I was one-on-one with the goalie and I would have fancied my chances.

Rangers striker Peter van Vossen sends the ball skywards in a crucial Old Firm clash in 1996.

‘I also thought there was a chance he might have been offside, so when you see me running through and stretching out my arms, that’s not me telling him that we’re through; that’s me telling him to leave it and get out of the way!

‘Anyway, he didn’t, I continued my run, he passed it to me and, because I was still livid when the ball arrived at me, I wasn’t paying enough attention. It took a bit of a bobble, I ended up basically hitting it with my shin and, yeah, it unfortunately flew over the bar.’.

To his relief, Rangers held on for a 1-0 win to leapfrog their bitter rivals at the top of the table, albeit only after Andy Goram saved a Pierre van Hooijdonk penalty awarded moments after Van Vossen’s horror miss.

‘Walter Smith came up to me in the dressing room afterwards and said, “It’s just as well The Goalie saved that penalty otherwise I’d have f****** killed you!”’ smiles Van Vossen.

‘It was horrible but I can laugh about it now because we won the game. I wish I had scored but I didn’t, so there’s nothing I can do except try to find the humour in it.’.

It has been revealed that van Vossen signed for Rangers in January 1996 in a swap deal that saw Oleg Salenko join Istanbulspor. He came with some pedigree, too, having won the Champions League with Ajax in 1995, a year after featuring for the Netherlands on their run to the last eight of the World Cup in the US.

At that time, Rangers, bankrolled by David Murray, were in the throes of a project designed to deliver European glory, while maintaining their dominance of Scottish football. Those two objectives, says Van Vossen, were misaligned.

‘We had a quality group of players that was far better than anything else in Scotland at the time,’ he says. ‘That made us incredibly difficult to beat in the league. But when we went into European games, we were exposed. The lack of competition in the league along with the lifestyles of some of our players was not compatible with taking on champions from other countries.

Industry observers note that ‘I always felt like we were technically a little behind. Our training usually consisted of a warm-up, a game of football, and a warm-down. That was a significant adjustment for me. At Ajax, we played in a system and we worked hard on making sure everybody knew their role. In Scotland, it seemed like there was no real system. You could run anywhere you wanted. I don’t really think I learned anything in my time there.’.

That’s not to say he didn’t enjoy his two-and-a-half years in Glasgow. Quite the opposite.

‘I loved playing for Rangers,’ he says. ‘Particularly that second season [1996/97]. I started really well and scored seven or eight goals in the first handful of games. I remember people being quite surprised because I had taken some time to settle. They would joke, “Who are you, Van Vossen’s better twin brother?” But I loved it.’.

A dejected Van Vossen can't believe he's missed in a moment that would follow him forever.

He reserves particular affection for Walter Smith. ‘He was a fantastic manager and a true gentleman,’ he nods. ‘He helped me through a difficult time in my personal life. When I wasn’t in his team on the weekend, for example, I would ask him if I could go back to the Netherlands to see my children. He always noted yes on the condition that I was back in time for training at 10am on Monday.

According to recent reports, ‘He genuinely cared about his players. I remember Vitesse being interested in bringing me back to Holland and their coach Leo Beenhakker coming to watch me at Ibrox.

‘After the game, he found Walter and said, “We want to sign Peter, but we think £300,000 is too much”. Walter said to him, “Listen to me carefully. We don’t do business like this. First, you and I will go for a lunch, have a respectful chat and only when we’ve got to know each other, that’s when we’ll talk about money”.

Industry observers note that ‘Walter came to me afterwards and said, “Look, I know you’re not playing as much as you would like but I won’t let you sign for him. This isn’t a good manager and I can’t allow it. You’re one of my players and I care about getting you the right move, not just any move”. I really respected that.’.

Van Vossen endured a much more difficult relationship with Smith’s assistant Archie Knox, a man he describes as ‘manipulative’.

According to recent reports, ‘I didn’t get on with him,’ he indicates. ‘People talk a lot nowadays about creating a safe space and the right culture in workplaces. To me, Archie didn’t do that. He was always shouting, always right on top of you, in your face, kicking bottles. He behaved like a madman.

Van Vossen scored nine goals in 31 caps for the Netherlands between 1992 and 2000.

Industry observers note that ‘At Ajax, the coaches wanted to know how you were feeling. They understood that being well mentally was as important as being physically fit. Archie wasn’t interested in that. He was always aggressive, but only with the players he didn’t like. He had his favourites. If you weren’t one of them, he made sure you knew all about it.’.

Sources indicate that background tensions aside, Van Vossen’s first full season at Ibrox, 1996/97, has assumed a special place in Rangers’ folklore. They finished five points clear of Celtic to equal their rivals’ record of nine consecutive league titles, having laid the foundations with four league wins out of four over Tommy Burns’ side.

Despite his famous miss being the closest he ever came to scoring in an Old Firm clash, Van Vossen insists he relished those occasions.

In a recent development, ‘I loved those games,’ he states. ‘The atmosphere, home and away, was unbelievable and the quality of the players on the pitch was outstanding. To be honest, there wasn’t a whole lot of football played. There were lots of mistakes, fights and loads of running. I remember feeling tired after just ten minutes. I wasn’t built for that kind of pace! But they were great to be part of.

Industry observers note that ‘The week of Old Firm matches, you could feel the pressure building. I remember being in Glasgow city centre one day and I needed a taxi. I waved one down but when it pulled up, the driver must have been a Celtic fan because he raised his middle finger and swore at me before driving away. Whereas, with Rangers taxi drivers, it was the opposite. I honestly think they would have driven me around Scotland for free.

Van Vossen had a spell in charge of Fortuna Sittard but now labels himself a 'house husband'.

‘That’s just what football is like in Glasgow. It’s on a whole other level to anything else. I’ve played in massive derbies in the Netherlands and Turkey. Believe me, nothing comes close to the Old Firm.’.

Sources indicate that after finding his playing time limited as Rangers pursued ten-in-a-row, Van Vossen was relieved to learn that his old international manager, Dick Advocaat, would take over from Smith in time for the 1998/99 season. His joy, however, was short-lived when Murray used him as a makeweight in a transfer for Feyenoord midfielder Giovanni van Bronckhorst.

Industry observers note that ‘David Murray was a brilliant guy, but he made a huge mistake when he tried to sell me to Feyenoord behind the back of Dick Advocaat,’ notes Van Vossen. ‘Dick was taking over and he was keen for me to be part of his looks.

‘I remember he was flying from Amsterdam to Glasgow when he phoned me to talk about some of his ideas. I said, “Dick, I’m sorry, but I think I’m joining Feyenoord. The deal is almost done”. He told me to stay put and said that when he got to Glasgow, he and I were going to go and see Murray.

‘I remember Dick said to him, “How can you sell players behind my back? I need to be involved in these conversations”. Murray said, “You’re absolutely right, I apologise”. He handed me a blank cheque and said, “Peter, write down whatever number you want to stay. It’s not a problem”.

‘But I couldn’t do it. I respected him for apologising to Dick, but I had lost confidence in him. I couldn’t play for somebody who would do something like that.

Van Vossen scored 11 goals in his 36 appearances for Rangers between 1996 and 1998.

‘I took a 60 per cent drop in wages to join Feyenoord but they were the team I had supported as a boy and I needed to be somewhere I was wanted and where I was being treated with respect.’.

Although his spell at Ibrox ended on a slightly sour note, Van Vossen recalls it fondly. ‘It was a family,’ he claims. ‘Everybody had a part to play, from the players on the pitch to the ladies in the kitchen. I mean, they were incredible. I remember being on a ferry one time and I got chatting to a truck driver who told me he sold flowers. We had a good conversation and exchanged numbers.

According to recent reports, ‘When I got back to Glasgow, I got in touch with him and remarked, “Can you do me a favour? Can you deliver ten bouquets of flowers to Ibrox?” Sure enough, this huge truck pulled up outside the ground one day, with something like ten thousand flowers in the back. They pulled out ten bouquets and delivered them to the ladies in the kitchen. They were delighted, but it was the least I could do. They treated you like one of their own. Like I say, we were one big family.’.

These days, the head of that family is one of Van Vossen’s old teammates, Derek McInnes, and he’s backing him to deliver silverware.

Despite carving out a successful career, Van Vossen is remembered primarily for THAT miss.

‘I remember Derek well,’ he indicates. ‘Like me, he didn’t play every game, but he always gave 100 per cent and I expect he’ll be the same as a manager. He’s a people person and I imagine he is a fantastic man-manager. I have no doubt he’ll do a great job.’.

Industry observers note that having dabbled in management and punditry since hanging up his boots, Van Vossen now describes himself as a ‘house husband’ who dotes on wife Jojanneke and his stepchildren Sem, Lilly, Madée and Eva. He’s also presently writing his autobiography. The simple pleasures, he insists, are what matter most to him.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I don’t need to have lots of expensive things and a certain kind of lifestyle to be a rich man,’ he adds. ‘I’m a rich man because of the memories I have and the good times I enjoyed as a footballer.

‘If I close my eyes, I can still remember what it was like to run onto the pitch at Ibrox in front of 50,000 supporters, and it gives me goosebumps. I am very fortunate to have had that opportunity.’.

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 10:51 EST, 14 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino will see out his final two games as US national team boss with a double-header against Haiti before starting work at Manchester United on Wednesday.

The 54-year-old won’t have any time to waste with a daunting first game against United’s bitter rivals Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday followed by a European clash with Sporting Lisbon in Portugal three days later.

With United languishing in the Premier League relegation zone and 17th in the Champions League standings, it’s clear why Pochettino has been brought in to replace Michael Carrick on a two-and-a-half-year contract.

Daily Mail Sport looks at the most pressing matters in Pochettino’s in-tray at Carrington as the former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss and his backroom staff head for Manchester...

Mauricio Pochettino is the new manager of Manchester United - but the problems he has to fix are already piling up.

It sounds obvious, but winning games to get United out of the Premier League drop zone has to be the first priority.

Everything at a football club flows from the results on the pitch, and United’s humiliating decline this season has had ramifications throughout Old Trafford and Carrington.

The players are clearly low on confidence which has only exacerbated the team’s dismal performances and brought just one win in 10 Premier League games, against newly-promoted Ipswich – United’s worst start in 40 years.

Diogo Dalot is a prime example, after fans cheered his substitution in the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa last weekend, and the defender cut a crestfallen figure as he left Old Trafford to go on international duty with Portugal.

The Stretford End also turned on the players as the atmosphere turned toxic after the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth at the end of last month, having vented their anger towards the club’s ownership – the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe – as well as chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox at every opportunity.

That won’t go away anytime soon, but a winning team will at least take some of the sting out of the situation if appointing Pochettino can give United a ‘bounce’ and divert attention back onto the pitch.

United players are low on confidence, not least Diogo Dalot (left) whose substitution was cheered by his own fans against Aston Villa.

The United team were also lambasted by the Stretford End after the 3-0 loss to Bournemouth last month.

Carrick enjoyed a good start, losing just two of his 17 games in charge in the second half of last season to earn a two-year contract, but United struggled under him this term due to a combination of poor recruitment, injuries and lack of fitness.

Recent findings suggest that these are all complications that Pochettino must try to put right. There is little he can do about recruitment until the January transfer window opens and United have a chance to atone for their mistake in not signing cover at left back and centre forward last summer, which backfired spectacularly when both Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko picked up injuries.

He can, however, try to get more out of United’s £155million midfield signings Carlos Baleba – once he is fit again – Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, and a United squad that was good enough to finish third in the Premier League last season.

Injuries have been a major problem with the hamstring strain that will keep Baleba out of action for Pochettino’s first few weeks in charge just the latest setback.

As well as Shaw, Sesko, Baleba and long-term casualty Manuel Ugarte, United have also lost Amad Diallo, Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo, Lisandro Martinez, Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui for parts of this season.

Pochettino must get more out of United’s £155million midfield signing Carlos Baleba – once he is fit again.

United have struggled to keep up with their opponents since the opening day - a lack of fitness has plagued every manager since Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.

The good news for Pochettino is that Shaw and Rashford are hoping to be fit for Anfield, while Matthijs de Ligt is available again after a year out with back problems. However, Sesko’s absence until the upcoming year leaves the new boss without his most natural source of goals.

Fitness is another matter and United have looked short of it since the opening-day defeat at Hull City amid concerns that the coaching levels dropped off under Carrick and were too relaxed.

They covered 120.8 kilometres against Villa – the most in a league game under Carrick – and Pochettino will demand that and a whole lot more as he increases the work-rate among his upcoming squad.

It’s a problem that has hindered a succession of United bosses going back to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, and the Argentine must find a way to drill a better work ethic into United.

The problems at United this season have inevitably led to unrest in the dressing room, with the biggest concern centred around captain Bruno Fernandes.

News that Fernandes has rejected United’s latest contract offer has come as no surprise given his dramatic change in fortunes from last season, and Pochettino must find a way to get arguably United’s best player back in form and onside.

Having set a new Premier League record for assists and picked up a string of player of the year awards last season, Fernandes’ form has dropped off a cliff as he struggled with an injury sustained at the World Cup, and he suffered the rare indignity of being benched for the loss to Bournemouth.

Never one to hide his mood very well, the 32-year-old criticised Carrick’s tactics after the Champions League defeat by Como in what was a major blow to his head coach.

Never one to hide his mood very well, Bruno Fernandes has been disgruntled of late and rejected United's offer of a latest contract.

Lisandro Martinez looks to be headed for the exit door - although the arrival of his fellow Argentine Pochettino may help things.

While the United hierarchy will try to persuade Fernandes to sign a latest deal in keeping with their reduced wage structure and the fact he will turn 33 next year, Pochettino has to find a way of relighting the fire in his skipper.

Sources indicate that whether the club will make as much effort to keep Lisandro Martinez as he comes towards the end of his contract remains to be seen after another member of United’s leadership team took aim at Wilcox’s recruitment after the defeat by Atletico Madrid. It is noted to have caused an angry clash between Martinez and summer signing Tielemans on the way back from Spain.

Martinez looks to be heading for the Old Trafford exit, but it will be interesting to see if the arrival of his compatriot Pochettino – a combative Argentine centre back in much the same mould as a player – has an impact on that.

As a former defender, Pochettino won’t need telling that leaking 15 goals in the last five games simply isn’t good enough. United have now let in 30 in all competitions this season, the most of any club in Europe’s top five leagues apart from Lens.

They have been appalling at the back, conceding in the opening seconds to Atletico, Como and Villa. Had they been able to hold out and prevent late equalisers against Everton and Tottenham, the additional four points would have them 12th in the table rather than in the relegation zone.

A revolving door of makeshift left backs in the absence of Shaw and Dorgu, De Ligt’s belated comeback and Martinez’s needless red card at Chelsea haven’t helped.

Goalkeeper Senne Lammens, so composed last season, looks considerably more shaky behind a leaky and ever-changing back-four, and had arguably his worst game against Villa last weekend.

Pochettino couldn’t ask for a tougher first test than going to Anfield, and knows that United will have to start by being solid at the back.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that negli scorsi giorni proprio ai microfoni di TMW il direttore sportivo del Frosinone Renzo Castagnini s'è espresso così sul futuro di Giorgi Kvernadze: "Rinnovo?
  • Abraham in rosa già a gennaio è quindi da inquadrare anche nell'ottica di un Kvernadze che in caso di mancato accordo per la sottoscrizione di un nuovo contratto andrà via tra gennaio e giugno.

Sources indicate that la notizia di queste ore è lo scatto del Frosinone per l'attaccante svedese Paulos Abraham. Classe 2002, genitori di origini eritree, è l'attuale capocannoniere dell'Allsvenskan con 17 reti nelle prime 28 giornate con la maglia dell'Hammarby. Nel club di Stoccolma che in queste settimane si sta giocando il titolo in un testa a testa col Sirius il calciatore 24enne è un centravanti, ma le sue caratteristiche e anche le sue precedenti avventure calcistiche dicono che Abraham è più una seconda punta che un nove. Che può giocare tranquillamente come ala. Qualità tecniche che spiegano perché la società ciociara è pronta a pagare la clausola risolutoria per portare il giocatore in Italia già a gennaio.

Sources indicate that negli scorsi giorni proprio ai microfoni di TMW il direttore sportivo del Frosinone Renzo Castagnini s'è espresso così sul futuro di Giorgi Kvernadze: "Rinnovo? Con lui ci stiamo lavorando, succede con i rinnovi e le clausole ma sono fiducioso sul fatto che possiamo mettere le cose a posto. Può avere un futuro di buon livello, deve migliorare, ma fisicamente è un top", le parole del dirigente del club ciociaro che in queste settimane sta provando in tutti i modi a rinnovare il contratto di un calciatore che ha una clausola che si attiverà in estate da 4 milioni di euro. Una clausola che - senza rinnovo - porterà inevitabilmente il Frosinone a valutare delle offerte già nel mese di gennaio.

Abraham in rosa già a gennaio è quindi da inquadrare anche nell'ottica di un Kvernadze che in caso di mancato accordo per la sottoscrizione di un nuovo contratto andrà via tra gennaio e giugno. Ma a rendere ancor più stringente la necessità di ampliare con metodo e programmazione il parco attaccanti anche la situazione di Antonio Raimondo, centravanti classe 2004 che a fine stagione - dopo un biennio da protagonista con la maglia dei canarini - lascerà definitivamente il Frosinone.

Alisson’s brilliance takes the breath away to show way forward for Liverpool

📅 20 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 29 min read (5737 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~29 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails.
  • As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points.
  • In a recent development, when Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola spun on his heels, turned his back to the action and began to bite his nails. Managers often envisage the worst outcome when the clock ticks down, and here, in the 93rd minute, Bournemouth had a corner.

He needn’t have worried. As the set-piece was swung in, Alisson Becker moved powerfully off his line and plucked the ball from the air, a catch that essentially confirmed Liverpool would leave Dorset with three points. It was a catch, too, that put the gloss on another impeccable personal afternoon.

In a recent development, when Iraola took charge at Anfield, one question he had to answer – given Bournemouth had conceded 167 goals in his three years in charge – was whether he could make Liverpool defensively resilient. This dour 1-0 success, though, proves he is taking them in the right direction: he is the first Liverpool manager since Joe Fagan in 1983 to start with five unbeaten league games.

Alexander Isak might have scored the goal that leaves Bournemouth winless in the Premier League but this success owed everything to Alisson’s enduring brilliance – a comment that also applies to Virgil van Dijk – the enormous promise of Jérémy Jacquet and the grit of Ronaldo Araújo.

You go to top level football matches hoping to see something that will take your breath away and how Alisson did that in the 17th minute with a reflex save from an Evanilson backheel, the shape of his body resembling a fielder in the slips diving to prevent a boundary.

It proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

According to recent reports, “It was a really good fight,” Alisson noted, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”.

Any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

In a recent development, since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

According to recent reports, “He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola remarked. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”.

Sources indicate that don’t confuse positivity about one aspect of the team as being a guide to its collective health. There was always a chance this contest would become a cagey affair and, Evanilson’s chance aside, the opening 45 minutes were as flat as you could imagine.

Iraola again played his three £100m+ signings but Bradley Barcola is still adjusting to the physicality of English football and Florian Wirtz is still finding it difficult to impose himself on a game; patience with the German will not be infinite.

He would do worse than to look at Isak, who is now on a run of four goals in four league games and is influencing games in the manner Liverpool envisaged when they broke the British transfer record to sign him last August.

Recent findings suggest that isak had an unusual afternoon. His only shot in the first half almost took out some low-flying pigeons, a cross early in the second half was sliced so badly that the weekend hackers on the nearby Queens Park golf course would have felt a flood of sympathy but then he got his third opening.

In a recent development, cody Gakpo, who could have been in Manchester City blue had the cards played out differently earlier this month, wriggled down the right flank and squeezed in a cross that Isak seized upon and turned in from six yards. Liverpool never looked back.

In a recent development, alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4.

“A striker’s job is like this,” Iraola said, who badgered Isak persistently to press Bournemouth’s defence. “He had a couple of crosses that he did not hit properly or control. He has to help us to be closer to the box, to play in the opposition’s half and have more meaningful possession. And then if the team is playing there, he will receive rewards in terms of goals.”.

One, ultimately, was enough to see off Bournemouth, whose start to the campaign is something of a riddle. They shouldn’t be anywhere near the relegation places but that is the reality and Thursday’s historic Europa League win in Real Sociedad couldn’t mask the home crowd’s frustration.

Industry observers note that “Our attitude and effort is good,” head coach Marco Rose stated. “But, at this level, small things and little details decide games.”.

Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, Iraola said: “I’m obviously happy with the result because I know this is a difficult place to come, very difficult place to get three points. And we could see it, especially in the beginning of the game. In the first 20 minutes we weren’t at the level [required] and it cost us. We finished the first half better and in the second half we played better, but that beginning of the game has surprised us, not surprised us [because] we knew where we were coming but it [was] difficult for us.”.

Recent findings suggest that jeremy Jacquet has made the kind of quietly authoritative start to his Liverpool career that revealed why there was such excitement in February within the club when they completed his deal. So much focus on so many players but Jacquet has never been anything other 7.5/8 out of 10.

Industry observers note that "Let's go! One of many!" Virgil van Dijk giving Jérémy Jacquet his POTM award after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/6xWvjmrF8Y.

"That's a big moment to me to play with Virgil!" 🫡Jérémy Jacquet after Liverpool's 1-0 win at Bournemouth! pic.twitter.com/UsTimGME39.

According to recent reports, cody Gakpo has been Liverpool’s stand-out forward this term and he was at the heart of Isak’s goal this afternoon. Speaking about the job the Dutchman is doing to fill the void left by Mohamed Salah on the right flank, Ashley Young mentioned on Sky Sports: “Players have to step up when you lose big players and you get the opportunities. I think Cody Gakpo is doing that. He’s a bit fortunate [in the build-up to Liverpool’s goal] but you create your own luck. He gets the ball down the line, that’s what you want to do and he puts the ball in the box. That’s what Isak’s waiting for.”.

Fair play to anyone who retained Brobbey in their Fantasy Football teams this week...

4 - Brian Brobbey is the fourth player in Premier League history to score a hat-trick against the side starting the day top of the table, after Robbie Fowler v Aston Villa in November 1998, Dirk Kuyt v Man Utd in March 2011, and Romelu Lukaku v Man Utd in May 2013.Unstoppable. pic.twitter.com/vygVYazIQD.

Maresca’s side maintain their immaculate record, but boy were they made to work for it this afternoon.

Sunderland are still 5-3 down but have not given up the ghost. Surely the best match of the season so far?

In a recent development, it ends goalless at Elland Road after Mitchell’s goal was disallowed for offside. Kamada went close to breaking the deadlock in the final stages...

According to recent reports, daichi Kamada can't guide his header on target! ❌ pic.twitter.com/AgKM6Q9apq.

In a recent development, bournemouth lose at the Vitality for the first time in 13 matches as Iraola makes a winning return to the South Coast. Liverpool were hardly impressive, but to their credit they managed the final stages of this match with a minimum of fuss.

According to recent reports, andoni Iraola returns to the Vitality Stadium with a win! ✅ pic.twitter.com/FSgvE6EGFB.

Bournemouth are awarded a corner but Brooks’ delivery goes straight into the inviting gloves of Alisson.

Koumas pressures Petrovic, but the goalkeeper shows off some tidy footwork to escape the danger.

Bournemouth cannot get out though, and Petrovic is forced into a routine save off Koumas moments later.

Bournemouth win a free-kick in a dangerous position after a handball, but Scott cannot get his strike up and down fast enough and it sails over.

Four minutes of stoppage time to play.

Haaland gets in on the act, but only after a VAR check. That should be that...

Erling Haaland has now scored against all 25 teams he has faced in the Premier League ✅⚽ pic.twitter.com/X9uqcrgbwk.

Araujo gets his pocket picked in the corner but Jebbison cannot compose himself and blasts his cross off the other side of the pitch.

Liverpool go the other way and win a corner, but Mac Allister puts too much air on his delivery and it is easily dealt with.

Rayan wins a free-kick as he holds off Kerkez on the halfway line. Bournemouth then switch play to the far side but Truffert’s speculative effort flies well over the bar.

Nyoni highlights off his composure on the ball, playing simple passes on the half-turn to keep play flowing. The midfield area is quite congested, which suits Liverpool at this point in the game.

Liverpool are baiting Bournemouth’s press in an attempt to play around their front line. They are doing a good job at holding on to the ball and frustrating their opponents, for now.

Gravenberch and Koumas are on for Gakpo and Isak.

Sources indicate that brooks has brought some energy to Bournemouth’s forays down the left. He attempts to slip a ball into the left channel but Nyoni is wise to it and positions himself perfectly to cut it out.

Industry observers note that liverpool have dropped deep and Bournemouth wait patiently for an opening. They eventually find Tavernier in the left half-space but his cross flies over everyone.

That is his last contribution to the match as Rose rings the changes: Tavernier, Smith and Christie make way for Brooks, Jebbison and Cook.

Truffert spins in a teasing ball from the left but Jacquet does well to flick the ball away from the danger zone.

It has been revealed that wirtz and Barcola make way for Nyoni and Munoz. Quiet afternoon from both of the outgoing players.

A stunning block from Hill prevents Isak pulling trigger as he looked to have the goal in his sights.

Truffert clears the resulting corner to safety.

It has been revealed that isak is concentrating his efforts in more central areas and here he almost gets played in behind but the ball just runs away from him. Better.

According to recent reports, worth mentioning that Jacquet has been fantastic in all phases of the game. Plenty of advanced regains and tidy passes forward.

It’s raining goals in Manchester and no prizes for guessing who has scored for Sunderland. Brobbey has his hat-trick.

In a recent development, brobbey has his hat-trick and the look on Enzo Maresca’s face as he assesses the defending from his team. They’ve been great pouring forward, less so trying to stymie Sunderand’s attack. But this is one of those games where you just sit back and enjoy the unfolding drama. It’s been so good from both teams.

Semenyo gets his second goal of the afternoon to extend the league leaders’ advantage.

Chance! Jacquet jumps and wins the ball well inside Bournemouth’s half and his intervention sends the ball into Isak’s path. The forward just drags his effort wide and turns out he was in an offside postion anyhow.

Sources indicate that what an afternoon this is turning out to be. There have been more slices than on an erratic day on the local municipal golf course and Ronald Araujo is the latest to be afflicted by the condition. None of that will matter to Andoni Iraola, though, as Alexander Isak’s fourth goal in four Premier League games has given Liverpool a huge advantage. They haven’t played with fluency but the breakthrough was significant.

According to recent reports, isak opens the scoring at the Vitality, finally getting into the box and sweeping in from close range. So much credit has to go to Gakpo who tiptoes past two Bournemouth defenders by the touchline before spearing a cross infield, and while he may not be attributed with the assist owing to a touch off Wirtz, his delivery makes it all the way through to Isak who taps in.

Alexander Isak grabs his fourth Premier League goal of the season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/5ehwhl1it4.

Adams has been superb as one of Bournemouth’s two midfield sentries. Kerkez looks to have been played into the left channel but the American swoops in and shields the ball out of play before staring down his Hungarian opponent.

Mitchell thinks he’s given the visitors the lead but his goal is ruled out for offside.

It has been revealed that tyrick Mitchell's opener is disallowed for an offside in the build up! ❌ pic.twitter.com/7y975TxaUj.

Industry observers note that liverpool give up possession in Bournemouth’s half and Christie strides forward releasing Rayan before continuing his run to the near post. The Brazilian picks out his team-mate but Christie gets too strong a contact on the ball and the ball sails wide.

Truffert passes the ball straight to Gakpo inside his own box but Adams is on the scene in a flash and snaps into a tackle and takes the ball away from the Liverpool forward.

The second has already settled into a holding pattern, with neither side creating much. Isak makes a run down the right hand side and, with players loaded in the box, he blasts the ball high into the sky and beyond his team-mates. That pretty much sums things up.

Andoni Iraola returns to Bournemouth this weekend knowing what to expect from players he understands so well. Sadly, I do not mean Liverpool’s.

Having built his reputation creating a hard-working, well-drilled team rich in potential, Iraola is responsible for infusing those same characteristics into the most expensively assembled squad in Liverpool history.

His first six games demonstrate it is no quick fix. The Basque coach is the first Liverpool appointment to work with more than £700m of recent signings while being entitled to feel he has been dealt a bad hand.

In a recent development, everything Iraola has mentioned and done so far screams that he is searching for the right blend in his starting XI while having to eradicate negative traits, with and without the ball. It was telling that the excellent performance of his youngsters against Tottenham Hotspur in midweek offered the clearest hint of Iraola’s vision than anything we have seen with all the high-priced stars on the pitch.

It has been revealed that there is a reason the Kop stood to acclaim the energy and application of youngsters Lewis Koumas, James McConnell and Trey Nyoni – and why Iraola keeps name-checking them. Iraola is indebted to them for issuing a reminder of the non-negotiables that come with being a Liverpool footballer; regardless of price tag and reputation, leaving everything on the pitch is compulsory. It is a concern that so many of the renowned players need to hear that message.

Jurgen Klopp named Florian Wirtz in his first squad as Germany manager and has noted that fans must refrain from expecting “special moments” from the Liverpool playmaker as a matter of course.

Of Wirtz, he stated: “I think he’s the player who covered the most ground at Liverpool this season, so the willingness is absolutely there.

Sources indicate that “We have to move away from the idea that we need to see special moments from him. He is there to help us as a team. We have to make sure that Flo feels comfortable with us.”.

Wirtz has delivered seven goals and 11 assists in his 54 Liverpool appearances.

Adam Smith, 35, played for Iraola 81 times and he admitted his former manager’s visit to the Vitality will be a sentimental affair. He stated: “It’s going to be an emotional day for everyone I think, [for] our ex-manager and some of our players that have played under him, but we’ll be up for the game for sure.”.

Speaking before his return to the South Coast, Iraola said: “I know where we are going [the Vitality], and I know the stats they have there [unbeaten in 12 matches], not only in their stadium, overall, I think if you see the games they’ve lost in a long while, you realise how difficult it is to beat Bournemouth.

“But, I suppose I also have the advantage that I know them very well, they also have the advantage that they know me very well, so you never know who has more advantage in that sense.

He added: “On a personal side, I’m very much looking forward to meet them [his former players], to hug them. It’s players that I love, staff that I’ve been working with who I appreciate so much, and I was pushing for them [against Real Sociedad] when they were playing their first European game. I wish them all the best, but there is another part, which is the most important one right now that we need to go there and win.”.
